魏老板还未答话，阿巧接口∶『哪个要他来做啥媒？我是不嫁的。』『咦！』魏老板看看妻子，又看看女儿，真有些莫名其妙了，『你们怎么想到这上头去了？』阿巧耳朵灵，心思快，立刻喜孜孜地问道∶『那末，他来做啥呢？』『他说要跟我谈一笔生意。』『谈生意？』他妻子问道∶『店里不好谈？』『我也是这么说。他说他一早起来一定要吃茶，不然没有精神。我就陪他去吃一回也不要紧。』『好，好！』阿巧推一推她父亲，『你老人家请！不过，只好谈主意，不好谈别的。』

Before he could answer, A’qiao broke in. “Who asked him to arrange any match? I am not getting married.” “Eh?” Wei looked from his wife to his daughter in genuine bewilderment. “How did you come to think of that?” Quick-eared and quick-witted, A’qiao brightened at once. “Then what has he come for?” “He says he wants to discuss a piece of business.” “Business?” his wife asked. “Can he not discuss it in the shop?” “That is what I said. But he says he must have his morning tea or he has no energy. There is no harm in my joining him for once.” “Very well!” A’qiao gave her father a little push. “Off you go, then. But you may discuss business only—nothing else.”

这一去去了两个钟头还不回来；阿巧心里有嘀咕，叫小徒弟到张胖子每天必到的那家茶店里去悄悄探望。须臾回转，张胖子跟魏老板都不在那里。这就显得可疑了。等到日中，依然不见魏老板的影子，母女俩等了好半天等不回来，只有先吃午饭。刚扶起筷子，魏老板回来了，满脸红光，也满脸的笑容。阿巧又是欣慰又是怨∶『到哪里去了？』她埋怨着∶『吃饭也不回来！』『张胖子请我吃酒；这顿酒吃得开心。』『啥开心？生意谈成功了？』阿巧问∶『是啥生意？』『不但谈生意，还谈了别样。是件大事！』魏老板坐下来笑道∶『你们猜得不错，张胖子是来替我们女儿做媒的。』听到这里，阿巧手足发冷；一下扑到母亲肩上，浑身抖个不住。

Two hours passed, and he did not return. Uneasy, A’qiao sent the little apprentice to make a discreet inquiry at the teahouse Zhang visited every day. The boy soon came back: neither man was there. This looked suspicious. By noon there was still no sign of Wei. Mother and daughter waited a long time, then decided to eat without him. They had just picked up their chopsticks when he appeared, his face flushed and wreathed in smiles. A’qiao was relieved but reproachful. “Where have you been? You did not even come home for lunch.” “Fatty Zhang invited me for a drink. A thoroughly enjoyable drink it was too.” “What was so enjoyable? Did you settle the business? What business was it?” “We discussed more than business. There was something else—something important.” Wei sat down, smiling. “You guessed correctly. Zhang did come to arrange our daughter’s marriage.” A’qiao’s hands and feet turned cold. She threw herself against her mother’s shoulder and shook from head to foot.

魏老板夫妇俩无不既惊且毫！问她是怎么回事？却又似不肯明说；只勉强坐了下来，怔怔地望着她父亲。到底知女莫若母，毕竟猜中了她的心事；急急向丈夫说∶『张胖子做媒，你不要乱答应人家。』『为啥不答应？』『你答应人家了！是怎么样的人家；新郎倌什么样子？』『新郎倌什么样子，何用我说？你们天天看见的。』

Both parents were startled and alarmed. They asked what was wrong, but she seemed unwilling to explain. With an effort she sat down again and stared at her father. No one knew a daughter better than her mother, who at last guessed what was troubling her. “You must not agree carelessly to a match Fatty Zhang proposes,” she told her husband urgently. “Why should I not agree?” “You have agreed already? What sort of family is it? What is the bridegroom like?” “Why should I tell you what he is like? You see him every day.”

提到每天看到的人，第一个想起的是间壁水果店的小伙计润生，做事巴结，生得也还体面；他有一手『绝技』，客人上门买只生梨要扦皮，润生手舞两把平头薄背的水果刀，旋转如飞，眼睛一霎的功夫，扦得干干净净，梨皮成一长条。陈巧最爱看他这手功夫；他也最爱看阿巧含笑凝视的神情。有一次看得出神失了手，自己削掉一小节指头；一条街上传为笑谈。以此话柄为嫌，阿巧从此总是避着他；但彼此紧邻，无法不天天见面，润生颇得东家的器重，当然是可能来求婚的。第二个想起的是对面香蜡店的小开，生得倒是一表人才，而且门当户对，可惜终年揭不得帽子；因为是个癞痢。阿巧想起来就腻味，赶紧抛开再想。

The first person A’qiao thought of was Runsheng, the young assistant at the fruit shop next door. He worked hard and was quite presentable. He also had a remarkable skill: if a customer bought a pear and wanted it peeled, Runsheng would set two thin-backed, flat-tipped fruit knives whirling in his hands. In the blink of an eye the pear was bare, its skin removed in one long strip. A’qiao loved to watch him do it, and he loved to see her gazing at him with a smile. Once he had become so absorbed in looking at her that his hand slipped and he sliced off a small piece of his finger. The whole street had made a joke of it. To avoid further gossip, she had kept out of his way ever since. But the shops were neighbors, so they could not help seeing each other daily, and his employer thought highly of him. It was quite possible that he had asked for her. The second person she thought of was the son of the incense-and-candle shop owner opposite. He was handsome, and their families were well matched, but he could never remove his cap: his scalp was diseased and patchy. The thought repelled her, and she hurriedly cast him from her mind.

这一想就想到阿祥了；顿时面红心跳。要问问不出口，好在有她母亲，『是哪个？』她问她丈夫。『还有哪个，自然是阿祥！』『祥』字刚刚出口，阿巧便霍地起身，躲了进去；脚步轻盈无比。魏老板楞了一会，哈哈大笑。『笑啥？快说！阿祥怎么会托张胖子来做媒？他怎么说？你怎么答复他？从头讲给我们听。』这一讲，连『听壁脚』的阿巧在内，无不心满意足；喜极欲涕，心里都有句话∶『阿祥命中有贵人；遇见胡道台这样的东家！』然而胡道台此时却还管不到阿祥的事；正为另一个阿巧在伤脑筋。

Then she thought of A’xiang. Her face flushed and her heart beat wildly. She could not bring herself to ask, but fortunately her mother could. “Who is it?” she asked her husband. “Who else? A’xiang, naturally.” The name had scarcely left his lips when A’qiao sprang up and fled into the back, her feet light as air. Wei stared for a moment, then burst into laughter. “What are you laughing at? Tell us! How did A’xiang come to ask Fatty Zhang to act as matchmaker? What did he say, and what did you answer? Begin at the beginning.” As the story unfolded, everyone—including A’qiao, listening from the other side of the wall—was entirely satisfied, so happy that tears seemed near. All shared the same thought: A’xiang had found a benefactor in an employer like Circuit Intendant Hu. Hu himself, however, could not attend to A’xiang’s affairs just then. Another A’qiao was giving him a headache.

阿巧姐昨夜通宵不归；一直到这天早晨九点钟才回家。问起她的行踪，她说心中气闷，昨天在一个小姊妹家谈了一夜。她的『小姊妹』也都三十开外了，不是从良；便是做了本家——老鸨。如是从了良的『人家人』，不会容留她只身一个人过夜；一定在头天夜里就派人送了她回来。这样看来，行踪就很有疑问了。于是胡雪岩不动声色地派阿祥去打听。阿巧姐昨天出门虽不坐家里轿子，但料想她也不会步行；所以阿祥承命去向弄堂口待雇的轿夫去探问。果然问到了；阿巧姐昨天是去了宝善街北的兆荣里，那轿夫还记得她是在倒数第二家，一座石库门前下的轿。所谓『有里兆荣并兆富，近接公兴，都是平康路』，那一带的兆荣里、兆富里、公兴里是有名的纸醉金迷之地；阿巧姐摒绝从人，私访平康，其意何居？着实可疑。

Sister A’qiao had been out all night and had not returned until nine that morning. Asked where she had been, she said she had felt depressed and spent the night talking at the home of an old friend. These “young companions” of hers were all over thirty now. They had either left the profession to marry or become proprietresses—in other words, madams. If she had visited a woman who had married into a respectable household, the family would hardly have kept an unaccompanied visitor overnight; someone would have escorted her home the evening before. Her movements therefore looked suspicious. Without betraying his thoughts, Hu sent A’xiang to investigate. She had not used the household sedan chair, but he did not imagine she had walked. A’xiang accordingly questioned the bearers waiting for hire at the mouth of the lane. He found what he wanted. She had gone to Zhaorong Lane, north of Baoshan Street. The bearer remembered setting her down at a stone-framed doorway, the second house from the far end. As the saying went, “Zhaorong and Zhaofu, with Gongxing close beside—all are roads to the pleasure quarters.” Those lanes were famous haunts of luxurious dissipation. Why had A’qiao dismissed her attendants and visited them secretly? It was deeply suspicious.

要破这个疑团，除却七姑奶奶更无别人。胡雪岩算了一下，这天正是她代为布置新居，约定去看的第四天；因而坐轿不到古家，直往画锦里而去。果然，屋子已粉刷得焕然一新；七姑奶奶正亲自指挥下人，在安放簇新的红木家具。三月底的天气，艳阳满院，相当燠热，七姑奶奶一张脸如中了酒似的，而且额上见汗，头发起毛，足见劳累。胡雪岩大不过意，兜头一揖，深深致谢；七姑奶奶答得漂亮∶『小爷叔用不着谢我，老太太，婶娘要来了；我们做小辈的，该当尽点孝心。』说着，她便带领胡雪岩一间屋子、一间屋子去看；不但上房布置得井井有条，连下房也不疏忽，应有尽有。费心如此，作主人的除了没口夸赞以外，再不能置一词。一个圈子兜下来，回到客厅喝茶休息，这时候胡雪岩方始开口，细诉阿巧姐一夜的芳踪；向七姑奶奶讨主意。

Only the Seventh Lady could solve the mystery. Hu counted the days: this was the fourth day since she had undertaken to furnish his new home, the day agreed upon for him to inspect it. He therefore took his chair directly to Huajin Lane instead of Gu’s house. Sure enough, the rooms had been repainted and looked entirely new. The Seventh Lady herself was directing the servants as they arranged brand-new rosewood furniture. It was late in the third month; brilliant sunshine filled the courtyard, and the weather was quite warm. Her face was flushed as if she had been drinking, her forehead beaded with sweat, and her hair coming loose. Plainly she had worked hard. Hu felt deeply indebted and made a profound bow of thanks. Her answer was graceful. “There is no need to thank me, Little Uncle. Your honored mother and my aunt—your wife—are coming. We of the younger generation ought to show our filial respect.” She led him through the house, room by room. Not only were the family apartments arranged in perfect order; even the servants’ quarters had been supplied with everything necessary. Such care left the owner nothing to do but praise it without reservation. After making the circuit, they returned to the drawing room to rest over tea. Only then did Hu explain A’qiao’s movements the previous night and ask for advice.

事出突兀，她一时哪里有主意？将胡雪岩所说的话，前前后后细想了一遍，觉得有几件事先要弄清楚。『小爷叔，』她问∶『阿巧姐回来以后，对你是啥样子？有没有发牢骚？』『没有，样子很冷淡。』『有没有啥收拾细软衣服，仿佛要搬出去的样子？』『也没有。』胡雪岩答说，『坐在那里剥指甲想心事，好象根本没有看到我在那里似的。』就问这两句话便够了。七姑奶奶慢慢点着头，自言自语似地说∶『这就对了！她一定是那么个主意！』由于刚才一问一答印证了回忆，胡雪岩亦已有所意会；然而他宁愿自己猜得不对，『七姐，』他很痛苦地问∶『莫非她跟她小姊妹商量好了，还要抛头露面，自己去「铺房间」？』『贱货！』脱口骂了一句。

The matter was so unexpected that the Seventh Lady had no ready answer. She considered his account from beginning to end and decided that a few points must first be clarified. “Little Uncle, how did she behave toward you when she came back? Did she complain?” “No. She was very cold.” “Did she pack any clothes or valuables, as though she meant to move out?” “No. She just sat there picking at her nails and thinking, as if I were not in the room.” Those two questions were enough. The Seventh Lady nodded slowly, almost talking to herself. “That fits. That must be her plan.” The exchange had revived Hu’s own recollections, and he too had begun to understand, though he would rather have been wrong. “Seventh Sister,” he asked painfully, “can she have arranged with her old companions to appear in public again—to open a courtesan establishment of her own?” A curse escaped him. “The shameless woman!”

『小爷叔！这，我要替阿巧姐不服。』七姑奶奶的本性露出来了，义形于色地说∶『一个人总要寻个归宿。她宁愿做低服小，只为觉得自己出身不是良家，一向自由惯了的，受不得大宅门的拘束，要在外头住；说起来也不算过分。这一层既然办不到，只有另觅出路；哪里来的还到哪里去，不也是顺理成间的事？就算是从良，总亦不能喊个媒波来说∶』我要嫁人了，你替我寻个老公来！「她」铺房间「自己不下水；遇见个知心合意的，自订终身，倒是正办。『听她一顿排揎，胡雪岩反倒心平气和了，笑笑说道∶』其实她要这样子做，倒应该先跟七姐来商量。『』跟我没商量！我心里不反对她这样子做；口里没有赞成她再落火炕的道理。阿巧姐是聪明人，怎么会露口风？我现在倒担心一件事；怕她心里恨你，将来会有意塌你的台。『』怎么塌法？『胡雪岩苦笑着，』只要她再落水，我的台就让她坍足了。『

“Little Uncle, there I must take her side.” The Seventh Lady’s nature asserted itself; righteous indignation showed in her face. “A person must find some settled place in life. She is willing to accept a subordinate position, but she feels that, having come from outside respectable society and been accustomed to freedom, she could not bear the restrictions of a great household. She wants to live separately. That is not an excessive request. If it cannot be granted, she must find another way. Is it not natural to return to the place she came from? Even if she wishes to marry, she can hardly summon a matchmaker and say, ‘I want a husband; find me one.’ She could open an establishment without taking clients herself. If she meets a suitable man who understands her, they can decide their own future. That would be a proper course.” After this scolding, Hu grew calmer. He smiled. “If that is what she means to do, she ought to have consulted you first.” “She has not consulted me. In my heart I might not oppose it, but I could hardly say aloud that I approved of her returning to that pit of fire. She is a clever woman. Why should she give me a hint? What worries me now is that she may resent you and deliberately damage your reputation afterward.” “How?” Hu smiled bitterly. “If she goes back into that life at all, my reputation will be damaged enough.”

『那还不算坍足。明天她挂上一块「杭州胡寓」的牌子，那才好看呢！』一句话说得胡雪岩发楞。他也听人说过，这一两年夷场『花市』，繁盛异常，堂子里兴起一种专宰冤大头的花样，找个初涉花丛，目炫于珠围翠绕；鼻醉于粉腻脂香；耳溺于嗷嘈弦管的土财主，筵前衾底，做足了宛转绸缪的柔态痴情；到两情浓时，论及嫁娶，总说孤苦伶仃一个人，早已厌倦风生，只为『身背浪向』有几多债务，只要替她完了债，她就是他家的人，除此别无要求。

“Not as badly as it could be. Suppose tomorrow she puts up a sign saying ‘The Hu Residence of Hangzhou.’ Then you will have something to look at!” Hu was stunned. He too had heard how, during the past year or two, the flourishing pleasure trade in the foreign settlement had developed a new device for fleecing wealthy fools. A provincial rich man, newly ventured among the flowers, would find his eyes dazzled by jewels and beauty, his nose intoxicated by powder and perfume, and his ears drowned in music. At the banquet and beneath the quilts, the woman would lavish tender, clinging affection upon him. When their feelings had ripened and marriage was mentioned, she would explain that she was lonely and without family, had long been weary of her life, and was held back only by debts incurred in the profession. If he paid those debts, she would belong to his household. She asked for nothing else.

于是冤大头替她还债『卸牌子』，自此从良。到一做了良家妇女，渐渐不安于室；百般需索，贪壑难填，稍不如意，就会变脸，三天一小吵，五天一大吵，吵得这家人家的上上下下，六神不安。冤大头这才知道上了恶当；然而悔之晚矣！少不得再花一笔钱，才能请她走路。这个花样名为『氵忽浴』。如果洗清了一身债务，下堂求去，两不相干，还算是有良心的；有些积年妖狐，心狠手辣，嫁而复出，还放不过冤大头，顶着他的姓接纳生张熟魏；甚至当筵诉说她的嫁后光阴如何如何？或者这家人家的阴私家丑，少不得又要花钱，才能无事。

The gullible patron would pay, have her signboard taken down, and bring her out of the profession. Once installed as a respectable wife, however, she would gradually become restless at home, making endless demands. Nothing could fill the gulf of her greed. Any slight disappointment brought a change of face; minor quarrels every three days and major ones every five left the entire household distraught. Only then would the victim realize how thoroughly he had been duped. But regret came too late. He would have to pay another sum to be rid of her. The trick was known as “taking a cleansing bath.” If, having washed away her debts, she left his household and broke off all dealings, she still had some conscience. Other hardened foxes were more ruthless. Returning to the profession after marriage, they refused to release their victim. They received new and familiar patrons alike under his surname, even recounting over dinner what married life in his house had been like, or exposing its private secrets and scandals. More money would then be needed to purchase peace.

不过，阿巧姐总不致于如此绝情。胡雪岩问道∶『她这样子做，于她有什么好处？她是理路极清楚的人；为啥要做这种损人不利己的事？』『小爷叔这句话说得很实在；阿巧姐应该不是这种人。事情到了这步田地，反倒好办了。小爷叔，你交给我，包你妥当。』七姑奶奶接着又说∶『小爷叔，你这两天不要回去！住在我这里，还是住在钱庄里；随你的便，就是不要跟阿巧姐见面。『胡雪岩实在猜不透她葫芦里卖的什么药？料知问亦无用；为今之计，只有丢开不管，听凭她去料理了。于是他说∶『我住在钱庄里好了。我请了张胖子做档手；趁这两天功夫陪他在店里谈谈以后的生意。』『张胖子为人倒靠得住的。就这样好了！你去忙你的生意；有事我会到阜康来接头。』

Surely A’qiao would not be so heartless. “What good would it do her?” Hu asked. “She is an exceptionally reasonable woman. Why would she harm another person without benefiting herself?” “That is a very fair point. She ought not to be that sort of person. Now that matters have reached this stage, they are easier to settle. Leave it to me, Little Uncle. I guarantee that I shall arrange everything properly. And do not go back for the next couple of days. Stay at my house or at the bank, whichever you please. Only do not see A’qiao.” Hu could not fathom her plan. He knew that questions would be useless; the only course was to put the matter aside and let her manage it. “I shall stay at the bank. I have engaged Fatty Zhang as a senior clerk. These two days will give me time to sit with him at the shop and discuss future business.” “Zhang is a dependable man. Very well. Attend to your business. If anything arises, I shall find you at Fukang.”

当天下午，七姑奶奶就去看一个人；是尤五的旧相知怡情老二。当年因为松江漕帮正在倒霉的时候，弟兄们生计艰难；身为一帮当家的尤五，岂可金屋藏娇？因而尽管怡情老二说之再三，尤五始终不肯为她『卸牌子』；怡情老二一气之下，择人而事，嫁的是个破落的世家子弟，体弱多病，不到两年呜呼哀哉。怡情老二没有替他守节的必要；事实上也不容于大妇，因而重张艳帜。先是做『先生』；后来做『本家』，跟尤五藕继丝连，至今不绝。

That afternoon the Seventh Lady went to see an old intimate of Brother You’s, the Second Miss of Yiqing House. Years earlier, when the Songjiang Grain-Boat Guild had fallen on hard times and its members could scarcely make a living, how could its leader establish a gilded nest for a favorite? However often the Second Miss urged him, Brother You had refused to redeem her from the profession. Angry, she had chosen another man, a sickly son of an impoverished distinguished family. He died within two years. She felt no obligation to remain a faithful widow; indeed, his principal wife would not tolerate her. She therefore returned to the pleasure quarters, first as a courtesan and later as a proprietress. Her ties with Brother You had never quite been severed and continued to this day.

阿巧姐原是怡情老二房间里的人；七姑奶奶去看怡情老二，一则是要打听打听阿巧姐预备复出，到底是怎么回事？再则也是要利用她跟阿巧姐旧日的情分，从中斡旋。不过自己一个良家妇女，为了古应春的声名，不便踏入妓家；特意到相熟的一家番菜馆落脚，托西崽去请怡情老二来相会。两个人有大半年不曾见面了。由于彼此的感情，一向很好，所以执手殷勤，叙不尽的寒温。怡情老二问讯了七姑奶奶全家，与尤五以外，也问起胡雪岩；这恰好给了她一个诉说的机会。『我今天就是为我们这位小爷叔的事，要跟你商量。』七姑奶奶说∶『阿巧姐跟胡老爷要分手了。』『为啥？』怡情老二讶然相问∶『为啥合不来？』『其实也没有啥合不来——。』七姑奶奶将家眷属脱困，将到上海；谈到阿巧姐的本心。语气中一直强调，脱辐已成定局，姻缘无可挽救。怡情老二凝神听完，面现困惑，『阿巧姐跟我，一两个月总要见一次面；这样的大事，她怎么不来跟我谈？』她问∶『她跟胡老爷分手以后怎么办？苏州又回不去；而且乡下她也住不惯的。』『是啊！』七姑奶奶接口说道∶『不管她怎么样，我们大家的情分总在的；就是胡老爷也很关心她。一个女流之辈，孤零零地，总要有个妥当的安顿之处才好。她自己好象打定了主意；不过，这个主意照我看不大高明。二阿姐，你晓不晓得她在兆富里有没有要好的小姊妹？』

A’qiao had once worked in the Second Miss’s establishment. The Seventh Lady sought her out partly to learn the truth about A’qiao’s supposed return to the trade and partly to enlist her old friendship as a means of mediation. But as a respectable married woman, she could not enter a courtesan house without compromising Gu’s reputation. She went instead to a familiar Western restaurant and asked a waiter to invite the Second Miss to meet her there. They had not seen each other for more than half a year. Their affection had always been strong, and they clasped hands warmly, with endless inquiries and greetings. After asking about the Seventh Lady’s family and Brother You, the Second Miss also asked after Hu, giving her visitor just the opening she needed. “It is on Little Uncle’s account that I want to consult you today. A’qiao and Mr Hu are going to part.” “Why?” the Second Miss asked in surprise. “Why can they not get along?” “There is really no quarrel between them—” The Seventh Lady explained that Hu’s family had escaped and was coming to Shanghai, then described A’qiao’s wishes. Throughout, she emphasized that the separation was settled and the relationship could not be saved. The Second Miss listened attentively, looking puzzled. “A’qiao and I meet every month or two. Why has she not discussed something so important with me? What will she do after leaving Mr Hu? She cannot return to Suzhou, and she is not used to country life.” “Exactly,” the Seventh Lady agreed. “Whatever she does, our friendship remains. Even Mr Hu is concerned for her. A woman alone must have somewhere suitable to settle. She seems to have made up her mind, but I do not think her plan is wise. Second Sister, do you know whether she has any close friends in Zhaofu Lane?”

怡情老二想了一下答说∶『有的。她从前没有到我这里来之前，在心想红老六那里帮忙；跟同房间的阿金很谈得来。阿金我也认识的，现在就住在兆富里，养着个小白脸。』『这个阿金，现在做啥？』『现在也是铺房间。』『我猜得恐怕不错。』七姑奶奶将阿巧姐瞒着人私访兆富里的经过，细细说了一遍，推断她是跟阿金在商量，也要走这条路。『奇怪！她为什么不来跟我商量？』『二阿姐，你问得对。不过，我倒要请问你，如果阿巧姐要走这条路，你赞成不赞成？』『我怎么会赞成？这碗饭能不吃最好不吃！』『那就对了。她晓得你不会热心，何必来跟你商量？』『这话倒也是。』怡情老二仍然困惑∶『我就不懂。她为啥还要回头来「触祭」这碗断命饭？』

The Second Miss thought for a moment. “Yes. Before she came to my establishment, she worked for the Sixth Miss of Xinxianghong House. She was very friendly with A’jin, who worked there too. I know A’jin as well. She lives in Zhaofu Lane now and keeps a handsome young lover.” “What does she do nowadays?” “She runs an establishment herself.” “Then I may have guessed correctly.” The Seventh Lady described A’qiao’s secret visit to Zhaofu Lane and explained her inference that she had gone to discuss following the same path. “How strange! Why did she not consult me?” “That is a fair question, Second Sister. But let me ask you: if A’qiao wanted to do such a thing, would you approve?” “How could I? Anyone who can avoid earning a living that way should do so.” “There you have it. She knew you would not be enthusiastic. Why should she consult you?” “That is true.” The Second Miss was still puzzled. “I simply cannot understand why she should return to that wretched livelihood.”

七姑奶奶认为要商量的正就是这一点。猜测阿巧姐预备重堕风尘的动机，不外三种∶第一是为生计所逼；第二是报复胡雪岩；第三是借此为阅人之地，要好好觅个可靠的人，为一世的归宿。『我在想，』七姑奶奶分析过后，谈她自己的意见∶『第一，她不必愁日子不好过，她自己跟我说过，手里有两三万银子的私房；而况分手的时节，胡老爷总还要送她一笔钱。至于说到报复，到底没有深仇切恨，要出人家的丑，自己先糟蹋名声出了丑；她不是那种糊涂人。想来想去，只有这样子一个理由∶想挑个好客人嫁！』『为了要嫁人，先去落水？这种事从来没有听说过。』怡情老二大为摇头，『除非象阿金那样，挑个小白脸养在小房子里；要挑好客人是挑不到的。』这话可以分两方面来听，一方面听怡情老二始终是不信阿巧姐会出此下策的语气；另一方面亦可以听出她不以阿巧姐此举为然。而无论从哪方面来听，都能使七姑奶奶感到欣慰的。

That, the Seventh Lady felt, was precisely what they must discuss. If A’qiao intended to return to the pleasure quarters, there could be only three motives: the need to support herself, revenge upon Hu, or a wish to use the place to meet men and find a dependable partner for life. Having analyzed the possibilities, she gave her own view. “First, she need not worry about money. She told me herself that she has twenty or thirty thousand taels put away. Besides, Mr Hu will certainly give her another sum when they part. As for revenge, there is no deep hatred between them. To disgrace him, she would first have to disgrace herself. She is not so foolish. The more I think of it, the more I can see only one explanation: she wants to choose a suitable patron to marry.” “Go back into that life in order to find a husband? I have never heard of such a thing.” The Second Miss shook her head vigorously. “Unless she means to follow A’jin’s example and keep some handsome young man in a little house. She will never find a good patron to marry that way.” Her words could be understood in two senses: she still did not believe that A’qiao would adopt such a poor plan, and she certainly disapproved of it. Either way, the Seventh Lady found them reassuring.

『二阿姐，我亦不相信七阿巧姐会走上这条路。不过，打开天窗说亮话，我一面是帮我小爷叔的忙；一面也是为阿巧姐的好。二阿姐，这件事上头，你要看我五哥的分上，帮一帮我的忙！』怡情老二有些不好意思地笑了，『七姑奶奶，说到这话，你该罚！你的吩咐，我还有个不听？』她质问着，『为啥要搬到五少来？』『是我的话说得不对，你不要动气。我们商量正经；我原有个主意——。』七姑奶奶是打算着一条移花接木之计，特地托号子里的秦先生，写信给宁波的张郎中，想撮合他与阿巧姐成就一头姻缘。这话说来又很长；怡情老二从头听起，得知张郎中如何与阿巧姐结识，以及后来落花有意，流水无情，怅然而返的经过，对此人倒深为同情。

“I too can hardly believe that A’qiao would take that road. But let us speak plainly, Second Sister. I am trying both to help Little Uncle and to do what is best for her. For Brother Five’s sake, you must help me with this.” The Second Miss smiled in embarrassment. “You deserve a penalty for saying that! Would I ever refuse something you asked? Why must you bring Fifth Master into it?” “I spoke wrongly. Do not be angry. Let us discuss the real business. I already had a plan—” The Seventh Lady intended to transplant the blossom onto another branch. She had specially asked Mr Qin at the firm to write to Dr Zhang in Ningbo, hoping to arrange a marriage between him and A’qiao. There was a long story behind it. The Second Miss listened from the beginning, learning how they had met and how the doctor, whose feelings had found no response, had returned home disappointed. She felt considerable sympathy for him.

『七姑奶奶，你这个主意，我赞成。不过，是不是能够成功，倒难说得很。男女之间，完全靠缘分；看样子，阿巧姐好象跟他无缘。』『不是！当初是因为我小爷叔横在中间，这面一片心都在他身上，张郎中再好也不会中意；那面，看阿巧姐是有主儿的，知难而退。其实，照我看，阿巧姐既然不愿意做人家的偏房，嫁张郎中就再好不过。第一，张郎中的太太最近去世了，以他对阿巧姐那一片痴情来说，讨她回去做填房，也是肯的；第二，张郎中年纪也不大。』七姑奶奶问道∶『阿巧姐今年多少？』『她属羊的。今年——，』怡情老二扳指头算了一下，失声惊呼∶『今年整四十了！』『她生得后生，四十倒看不出。不过总是四十了！』七姑奶奶停了一下，歉然地说∶『二阿姐，我说一句你不要生气，四十岁的人，又是这样子的出身；只怕要做人家的正室，不大容易！』『岂止不大容易？打着灯笼去找都难。』怡情老二很郑重地问道∶『七姑奶奶，张郎中那里，你有几分把握？』『总有个六七分。』『六七分是蛮有把握的了。我今天就去看阿巧姐，问她到底是啥意思？如果没有这样的打算，自然最好；倘使有的，我一定要拦住她。总而言之，不管她怎么样打算，我一定要做个媒。』『你是女家的媒人，我是男家的。我们一定拿它做成功也是件好事。』

“I approve of your plan. But whether it can succeed is another matter. Between a man and a woman, everything depends on affinity, and A’qiao does not seem to have any with him.” “That is not it. Little Uncle stood between them. Her whole heart was fixed on him, so however good the doctor might be, she would never consider him. The doctor, for his part, saw that she already belonged to someone and withdrew before the obstacle. As I see it, if she is unwilling to become a concubine, she could do no better than marry him. First, his wife has recently died. Given his devotion to A’qiao, he would be willing to take her as his new principal wife. Second, he is not very old. How old is A’qiao now?” “She was born in the year of the Sheep. This year—” The Second Miss counted on her fingers, then exclaimed in surprise. “Exactly forty!” “She looks young; one would never guess forty. But forty she is.” The Seventh Lady paused, then added apologetically, “Do not be offended, Second Sister, but a woman of forty, with her background, cannot easily become a man’s principal wife.” “Not easily? One could hardly find such a match with a lantern. Tell me seriously: how certain are you of the doctor?” “Six or seven chances in ten, at least.” “That is fairly certain. I shall see A’qiao today and ask what she means to do. If she has no intention of returning to the trade, so much the better. If she has, I must stop her. Whatever she intends, I shall act as matchmaker.” “You will represent the bride, and I the groom. We must make it succeed. It will be a good deed.”

『当然是好事。不过，好象委屈了张郎中。』提到这一层。七姑奶奶想起自己嫁古应春以前，由胡雪岩居间安排，拜王有龄的老太太做义女的往事，顿时又有了灵感。『二阿姐，既然你这样说，我们倒商量商量看，怎么样把阿巧姐的身分抬一抬？』七姑奶奶的安排是，请胡老太太收阿巧姐为义女；于是胡雪岩便是以『舅爷』的身分唱一出『嫁妹』了。这原是古人常有之事，在此时此地来说，特别显得情理周至，怡情老二自然赞成，也为阿巧姐高兴，认为这样子做，她倒是『修成正果』了。

“A good deed, certainly. Though it seems rather unfair to the doctor.” At that, the Seventh Lady remembered how, before she married Gu, Hu had arranged for Wang Youling’s mother to adopt her as a daughter. Inspiration came at once. “Since you feel that way, Second Sister, let us consider how to raise A’qiao’s standing.” Her plan was to ask Hu’s mother to adopt A’qiao. Hu would then take the part of a brother marrying off his sister, receiving the honors due to the bride’s brother. Such arrangements had often been made in former times. In their present circumstances, it seemed a particularly considerate and reasonable solution. The Second Miss naturally approved and rejoiced for A’qiao: through this, she thought, her long journey would reach a proper fulfillment.

七姑奶奶也很得意于自己的这个打算；性子本来急，也正兴头的时候，当时就要邀怡情老二一起去看阿巧姐，当面锣、对面鼓，彻底说个明白。倒还是怡情老二比较持重，认为应该先跟阿金碰个头，打听清楚了邀她一起去谈，更容易使阿巧姐受劝。『那也好！』七姑奶奶问道∶『我们就去看阿金。』『这——，』怡情老二知道阿金因为养着小白脸，忌讳生客上门；但这话不便明说，所以掉个枪花∶『七姑奶奶，你的身分不便到她那里。我叫人去喊她来。』于是她唤带来的小大姐，赶到兆富里去请阿金；特别叮嘱喊一乘『野鸡马车』，坐催阿金一起坐了来。在这等候的当儿，少不得又聊家常。怡情老二的话中，颇有厌倦风尘之意；但也不曾表示要挑个什么样的人从良，七姑奶奶思路快，口也快，听出她的言外之意，忍不住要提出诤劝。

The Seventh Lady herself was delighted with the idea. Impatient by nature and now carried away by enthusiasm, she wanted to take the Second Miss straight to A’qiao and settle the whole matter face to face. The Second Miss was more cautious. She thought they should first see A’jin, establish the facts, and invite her to join them; A’qiao would then be more easily persuaded. “Very well. Let us go and see A’jin.” “Well—” The Second Miss knew that A’jin disliked unfamiliar visitors because she kept a young lover, but she could hardly say so outright. She changed tack. “A woman of your standing should not go there. I shall send for her.” She called the young maid who had accompanied her and sent her hurrying to Zhaofu Lane, with particular instructions to hire an ordinary street carriage and bring A’jin back in it without delay. While they waited, the two women naturally talked of their own affairs. The Second Miss sounded weary of life in the pleasure quarters, yet said nothing of choosing a man to marry. Quick in both thought and speech, the Seventh Lady heard what lay beneath her words and could not resist offering candid advice.

『二阿姐，你不要一门心思不转弯，那样也太痴了！你始终守着我五哥，守到头发白也不会成功。这里头的原因，五哥想必跟你说过。他领一帮，做事要叫人心服；弟兄穷得没饭吃，他还要多立一个门户，你想，这话怎么说得过去？二阿姐，你死了这条心吧！』怡情老二无词以对。默然泫然，惟有背人拭泪。七姑奶奶也觉得心里酸酸地好不自在；倒有些懊悔，不该拿话说得这么直。『说真的，』她没话找话，用以掩饰彼此都感到的不自然，『那位张郎中倒是好人，家道也过得去；我就怎么没有想到，早应该替你做这个媒。』『多谢你，七姑奶奶！命生得不好，吃了这碗断命饭；连想做小都不能够，还说啥？』话中依然是怨怼之意。使得一向擅于词令的七姑奶奶也无法往下接口了。

“Second Sister, do not fix your mind on a single course and refuse to turn aside. That is too foolishly devoted. If you go on waiting for Brother Five, you may wait until your hair is white and still achieve nothing. He must have told you why. He leads a whole guild and must act in ways that earn its members’ respect. While they are too poor to feed themselves, how could he justify setting up another household? Give up that hope.” The Second Miss had no answer. Silent and tearful, she turned away to wipe her eyes. The Seventh Lady too felt an ache of unhappiness and regretted having spoken so plainly. “Truly,” she said, searching for something to ease their mutual embarrassment, “that doctor is a good man, and comfortably off. Why did I not think of it? I ought to have arranged a match for you long ago.” “Thank you. But I was born to ill fortune and took up this wretched livelihood. I cannot even become a concubine. What more is there to say?” Her words still held resentment, and the usually eloquent Seventh Lady could find nothing to add.

幸好，兆富里离此不远；一辆马车很快地去而复回，载来了阿金。她在路上便已听小大姐说过，所以一见七姑奶奶，不必怡情老二引见，很客气地问道∶『是尤家七姑奶奶？生得好体面！』『不敢当！这位，』七姑奶奶问怡情老二，『想来就是阿金姐了？』『是啊！』怡情老二做主人，先替阿金要了食物饮料；然后开门见山地说∶『七姑奶奶为了关心阿巧姐，特意请你来，想问问你；这两天阿巧姐是不是到你那里去了？』『她常到我那里来的。』『阿金姐，』七姑奶奶说，『我们是初会，二阿姐知道我的，心直口快。我说话有不到的地方，请你不要见气。』这是因为阿金跟怡情老二，谈到阿巧姐时，一上来便有针锋相对之势；七姑奶奶深怕言事碰僵，不但于事无补，反倒伤了和气，所以特为先打招呼。阿金也是久历风尘，熟透世故的人，自知一句『她常到我这里来的』答语，语气生硬，隐含敌意，成为失言；所以歉然答道∶『七姑奶奶你言重了！我的嘴笨；二阿姐又是好姊妹，说话不用客气。你可千万不能多我的心！』既然彼此都谦抑为怀，就无须再多作解释，反倒象真的生了意见。不过，有些话，七姑奶奶因为彼此初交，到底不便深问；要由怡情老二来说，比较合适。因而报以一笑之外，向旁边抛了个眼色示意。

Fortunately, Zhaofu Lane was nearby. The carriage soon returned with A’jin. The maid had explained matters on the way, so A’jin needed no introduction before greeting the Seventh Lady courteously. “You are the Seventh Lady of the You family? What a fine-looking woman you are!” “You are too kind.” The Seventh Lady turned to her companion. “Then this must be Sister A’jin?” “Yes.” Acting as hostess, the Second Miss ordered food and drink for the newcomer, then came straight to the point. “The Seventh Lady is concerned about A’qiao and has specially asked you here. Has A’qiao been to see you these past few days?” “She comes to see me often.” “Sister A’jin,” the Seventh Lady said, “we have not met before, but Second Sister knows me: I am frank and speak my mind. If I say anything clumsy, please do not take offense.” A’jin and the Second Miss had seemed at odds as soon as A’qiao was mentioned. The Seventh Lady feared that a collision would accomplish nothing and only damage their friendship, so she made this precautionary apology. A’jin too had long experience of the world and understood its ways. She knew that her stiff answer had carried a hint of hostility and had been ill judged. “Please do not say that. I am clumsy with words. Second Sister and I are old friends, so I do not stand on ceremony with her. You must not misunderstand me.” With both sides showing humility, further explanations would only suggest that there really was a quarrel. Still, as a new acquaintance, the Seventh Lady could hardly press certain questions herself. The Second Miss would be better placed to ask them. She smiled and gave her a meaningful glance.

怡情老二点点头，接下来便用平静的语气，向阿金说明原委∶『阿巧姐跟胡老爷生了意见。「清官难断家务事」，谁是谁非也不必去说它；总而言之，恐怕是要分手了。七姑奶奶跟阿巧姐的感情一向是好的；当初作成他们的姻缘，又是七姑奶奶出过力的，不管怎么说，阿巧姐的事，她不能不关心。刚刚特地寻了我来问我；我实在不晓得。阿巧姐好久没有碰过头了，听说这两天到你那里去过，想必总跟你谈了，她到底有什么打算？』『喔，』阿金听完，不即回答，却转脸问七姑奶奶，『阿巧姐跟胡老爷的感情，到底怎么样？』『不坏啊！』

The Second Miss nodded and explained calmly to A’jin. “A’qiao and Mr Hu have fallen out. Even a wise magistrate cannot settle family troubles, so there is no need to decide who is right or wrong. In short, they will probably separate. The Seventh Lady has always been close to A’qiao and helped bring them together in the first place. Naturally, she cannot be indifferent to what happens now. She came specially to ask me, but I know nothing. I have not seen A’qiao for some time. Hearing that she had visited you in the last few days, I thought she must have told you something. What does she intend to do?” “Oh.” A’jin did not answer immediately. Instead, she turned to the Seventh Lady. “How are things really between A’qiao and Mr Hu?” “Not bad.”

『那就奇怪了！』阿金困惑地，『她每次来，总怨自己命苦。我问她∶胡老爷待你好不好？她总是摇头不肯说。看样子——。』下面那句话，她虽不说，亦可以猜想得到。这一下，却是轮到七姑奶奶有所困惑了；『阿巧姐为啥有这样的表示？』她问，『他们要分手，也是最近的事；只为胡老爷的家眷要到上海来了，大太太不容老爷在外面另立门户，阿巧且又不肯进她家的门，以致于弄成僵局。要说以前，看不出来他们有啥不和的地方！』阿金点点头，『这也不去说它了。』她的脸色阴沉了，『也许要怪我不好。我有个堂房姑婆，现在是法华镇白衣庵的当家师太；一到上海，总要来看我，有时候跟阿巧姐遇见，两个人谈得很起劲。我们那位老师太，说来说去无非「前世不修今世苦」，劝她修修来世。这也不过出家人的老生常谈；哪知道阿巧姐倒有些入迷的样子。』一口气说到这里，七姑奶奶才发觉自己的猜想完全错了！照这段话听来，阿巧姐去看阿金，或者与那位师太有关；不是为了想铺房间。因而急急问道∶『怎样子的入迷？』『说起来真教人想不到。她那天来问我白衣庵的地址，我告诉了她；又问她打听地址何用？她先不肯说，后天被逼不过，才说实话∶要到白衣庵去出家！』七姑奶奶大惊失色∶『做尼姑？』

“Then it is strange.” A’jin looked puzzled. “Whenever she comes, she complains of her unhappy fate. I ask whether Mr Hu treats her well, but she only shakes her head and refuses to say. From the look of things—” She left the next words unspoken, though their meaning was easy to guess. Now the Seventh Lady was puzzled in turn. “Why should she give that impression? This talk of parting is very recent. Mr Hu’s family is coming to Shanghai, and his principal wife will not allow him to keep a separate household. A’qiao refuses to enter the family home, so they are at an impasse. Before this, I could see no sign of disagreement between them.” A’jin nodded. “Let us leave that aside.” Her face grew gloomy. “Perhaps I am to blame. I have a great-aunt on my father’s side, from a collateral branch of the family. She is now abbess of White-Robed Convent in Fahua Town. Whenever she comes to Shanghai, she visits me. Sometimes she has met A’qiao here, and they have talked with great enthusiasm. The old abbess is always saying that suffering in this life comes from a failure to cultivate virtue in the last, and urging her to prepare for a better life to come. It was only the usual talk of a religious person. Who could have thought A’qiao would become so absorbed in it?” Only then did the Seventh Lady realize that her guesses had been entirely wrong. A’qiao’s visit might have concerned the abbess, not the opening of a courtesan establishment. “What do you mean, absorbed?” she asked urgently. “It is quite unexpected. The other day she asked me for the address of White-Robed Convent. I told her, then asked why she wanted it. At first she would not say. When I pressed her, she finally admitted that she wanted to enter the convent and leave the world.” The Seventh Lady’s face changed with shock. “Become a nun?”

『哪个晓得呢？』阿金忧郁地答道∶『我劝了她一夜，她始终也没有一句确实的话；是不是回心转意了，哪个也猜不透。』『我猜不会的。』怡情老二却有泰然的神情，『阿巧姐这许多年，吃惯用惯从没有过过苦日子。尼姑庵里那种清苦，她一天也过不来。照我看——。』她不肯再说下去；说下去话就刻薄了。照七姑奶奶想，阿巧姐亦未必会走到这条路上去。自宽自慰之余，却又另外上了心事；她不愿重堕风尘，固然可以令人松一口气，但这种决绝的样子，实在也是抓住胡雪岩不放的表示。看起来麻烦还有的是。『现在怎么办呢？』七姑奶奶叹口气说，『我都没有招数了。』怡情老二跟她交往有年，从未见她有这样束手无策的神情。一半是为她，一半为阿巧姐，自觉义不容辞地，在此时要出一番力。

“Who can tell?” A’jin answered unhappily. “I spent the whole night trying to persuade her out of it, but she never gave me a definite answer. No one can guess whether she changed her mind.” “I do not think she will do it,” the Second Miss said calmly. “For all these years she has been accustomed to comfort and has never lived a hard life. She could not endure the austerity of a convent for a single day. As I see it—” She stopped. To go on would have been unkind. The Seventh Lady too thought A’qiao might not take that road. Yet even as she comforted herself with this thought, another worry arose. It was a relief that A’qiao did not intend to return to the pleasure quarters. But such a drastic gesture also showed that she would not release her hold upon Hu. There seemed to be plenty of trouble still ahead. “What are we to do now?” she sighed. “I have no more ideas.” In all their years of friendship, the Second Miss had never seen her so helpless. Partly for her sake and partly for A’qiao’s, she felt bound to make an effort.

『阿巧姐落发做尼姑是不会的，无非灰心而已！我们大家为她好，要替她想条路走！』怡情老二向阿金说∶『她今年整四十岁了，这把年纪，还有啥世面好混？七姑奶奶预备替她做个媒——。』听她谈完张郎中，阿金亦颇为兴奋∶『有这样的收缘结果，还做啥尼姑！』她说，『难得七姑奶奶热心；我们跟阿巧姐是小姊妹，更加应该着力。这头媒做成功，实在是你阴功积德的好事。我看我们在这里空谈无用，不如此刻就去看她，我不相信三张嘴说不过也一个。

“A’qiao will not shave her head and become a nun. She is only disheartened. We all want what is best for her, and we must find her a way forward.” The Second Miss turned to A’jin. “She is exactly forty this year. At that age, what future has she in this world of ours? The Seventh Lady is proposing a marriage—” When A’jin had heard the story of Dr Zhang, she too grew excited. “With such a proper ending in prospect, why become a nun? How good of the Seventh Lady to take such trouble! We are A’qiao’s old companions and ought to work even harder. Bringing this match about would be a true deed of merit. There is no use sitting here talking. Let us go and see her now. I refuse to believe that the three of us cannot persuade one woman.”

由于怡情老二与阿金很起劲，七姑奶奶的信心也恢复了，略想一想问道∶『阿金姐，二阿姐，你们是不是决心要帮阿巧姐的忙？』『自然。』怡情老二说，『只要帮得上。』『好的！那么两位听我说一句。凡事事缓则圆；又道是只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针，从今天起。索性叫胡老爷不必再跟阿巧姐见面；我们先把她的心思引开来，让她忘记有姓胡的这个人。这当然不是三天两天的事，所以我要先问一问两位；真要帮她的忙，一定要花功夫下去。从今天起，我们三个嬲住她，看戏听书吃大菜，坐马车兜风，看外国马戏，凡是好玩的地方，都陪她去；好不肯去，就说我们要玩。人总是重情面的，她决计不好意思推辞；也不好意思哭丧了脸扫大家的兴。到夜里我们分班陪着她住在一起，一面是看住她；一面是跟她谈天解闷。这样有半个月二十天下来，她的心境就不同了；到那时候再跟她提到张郎中，事情就容易成功！至于这些日子在外头玩儿的花费，我说句狂话，我还用得起，统通归我！』『二阿姐！』阿金深深透口气，『七姑有奶这样子的血性；话说到头了，我们只有依她。不过，也不好七姑奶奶一个人破费。』『当然。』怡情老二向七姑奶奶说∶『什么都依你，只有这上头，请你不要争，大家轮着做东；今天是我。我们走吧，邀她出来看「杨猴子」。』于是由怡情老二结了帐，侍者将帐单送了来，她在上面用笔画了一个只有她自己认得的花押。这原是西洋规矩，名为『签字』，表示承认有这笔帐；本来要写名字，如果不识字的，随意涂一笔也可以，应到规矩就行了。

Their enthusiasm restored the Seventh Lady’s confidence. After a little thought she asked, “Sister A’jin, Second Sister, are you determined to help A’qiao?” “Naturally,” the Second Miss replied, “if we can.” “Good. Then listen to me. Matters settle more smoothly when one takes time. And with sufficient effort, an iron pestle can be ground into a needle. From today, let Mr Hu stop seeing her altogether. We shall first divert her thoughts and make her forget that such a person exists. That cannot be done in two or three days, which is why I had to ask you first. If we truly mean to help, we must devote time to it. Beginning today, the three of us will keep her company constantly. Plays, storytelling, Western dinners, carriage rides, foreign circuses—wherever there is something enjoyable, we shall take her. If she refuses, we shall say that we want to go. People care about their friends’ feelings. She will be too embarrassed to refuse and too considerate to spoil everyone’s pleasure with a gloomy face. At night we shall take turns staying with her, both to watch over her and to talk and ease her mind. After fifteen or twenty days of that, her mood will change. Then we can mention Dr Zhang, and success will be much easier. As for the cost of these outings, let me boast a little: I can still afford it. I shall pay for everything.” A’jin drew a deep breath. “Second Sister, with such generosity, the Seventh Lady has said all there is to say. We can only follow her lead. But we cannot let her bear all the expense.” “Of course not.” The Second Miss turned to the Seventh Lady. “We shall do everything as you say, except on that point. Do not argue. We shall take turns as hostess, and today is mine. Come, let us invite her out to see the foreign circus.” She signed for the bill, putting a personal flourish on the account the waiter brought, a mark intelligible only to herself. This was a Western custom called “signing,” an acknowledgment of the debt. Ordinarily one wrote one’s name; an illiterate person could make any distinctive mark, provided the proper form was observed.

三个人都带着小大姐，挤上两辆『野鸡马车』，直放阿巧姐寓处∶下车一看，便觉有异，大门开了一半，却无人应门。七姑奶奶便提高了声音喊道∶『阿祥、阿福！』阿祥、阿福都不见，楼梯上匆匆奔下来一个人，晃荡着长辫子，满脸惊惶；是阿巧姐的丫头素香。

Each woman had brought a young maid. They crowded into two hired street carriages and drove straight to A’qiao’s lodgings. On getting out, they immediately sensed something wrong. The front door stood half open, but no one answered. The Seventh Lady raised her voice. “A’xiang! A’fu!” Neither appeared. Instead, someone hurried down the stairs, her long braid swinging, her face full of alarm. It was Suxiang, A’qiao’s maid.

三个人面面相觑，都猜到了是怎么回事？七姑奶奶遇到这种情形，却很沉着，反安慰她说∶『素香，你不要急！有话慢慢说。』『奶奶不见了！』素香用带哭的声音说，『不晓得到哪里去了？』叫她慢慢说，她说得还是没头没脑，七姑奶奶只好问道∶『你怎么知道你奶奶不见了？她什么时候出的门？』『老爷一走，没有多少时候，她叫我到香粉弄去买丝线；又差阿祥去叫米叫柴。等到我跟阿祥回来，她已经不知道什么时候出门了；连门上都不知道，再看后门；是半开在那里。一直到下半天三点钟都不见回来；我进房去一看，一只小首饰箱不见了，替换衣服也少了好些。这——这——！』素香着急地，不知如何表达她的想法。这不用说，自然是到老师太那里去了。七姑奶奶倒吸一口冷气，怔怔地望着同伴；怡情老二便问∶『素香，你们老爷知道不知道？』『不知道。』素香答说∶『阿祥跟轿班去寻老爷去了。』『你们老爷在钱庄里。』七姑奶奶说，『你看，轿班还有哪个在？赶快去通知；请你们老爷到这里来，我有要紧话说。』

The three women exchanged glances. Each guessed what had happened. In such a situation the Seventh Lady remained calm and even comforted the maid. “Suxiang, do not be frightened. Tell us slowly.” “Madam has disappeared!” Suxiang said, almost in tears. “No one knows where she has gone.” Asked to speak slowly, she still began in the middle of the story. The Seventh Lady had to question her. “How do you know she has disappeared? When did she leave?” “Not long after Master went out, she sent me to buy silk thread in Xiangfen Lane and sent A’xiang to order rice and firewood. When we came back, she had already gone. No one knew when she had left, not even the man at the front door. Then we looked at the back door and found it half open. By three this afternoon she still had not returned. I went into her room: a small jewelry box was missing, and quite a few changes of clothes. That—that—” Too anxious to explain, Suxiang faltered. There was no need to say it: she must have gone to the elderly abbess. The Seventh Lady drew in a sharp breath and stared at her companions. The Second Miss asked, “Suxiang, does your master know?” “No. A’xiang and the chairmen have gone to look for him.” “Your master is at the bank,” the Seventh Lady said. “See whether any of the chairmen are still here. Send someone to tell him at once. Ask him to come here; I have something important to say.”

就在这时候，雪岩已经赶到；同来的还有萧家骥。胡雪岩跟怡情老二熟识，与阿金却是初见，不过此时亦无暇细问，同时因为有生客在，要格外镇静，免得『家丑』外扬，所以只点点头，平静地问∶『你们两位怎么也来了？』『我们是碰上的。』七姑奶奶答说，『有话到里面去说。』进入客厅，她方为胡雪岩引见阿金。话要说到紧要地方了，却不宜让素香与阿祥听到；所以她要求跟胡雪岩单独谈话。『阿巧姐去的地方，我知道，在法华镇，一座尼姑庵里，事不宜迟，现在就要去寻她。我看，『七姑奶奶踌躇着说，』只好我跟阿金姐两个人去；你不宜跟她见面。『胡雪岩大惑不解，』到底怎么回事？『他问∶』何以你又知道她的行踪？那位阿金姐，又是怎么回事？『『这时候没有办法细说。小爷叔，你只安排我们到法华好了。』

At that moment Hu arrived, accompanied by Xiao Jiaji. He knew the Second Miss well but had never met A’jin. There was no time for inquiries; indeed, the presence of a stranger made him all the more determined to remain composed and keep his domestic troubles from becoming public. He merely nodded and asked quietly, “How do you two come to be here as well?” “We happened to meet,” the Seventh Lady replied. “Let us talk inside.” In the sitting room she introduced A’jin. They were approaching matters that Suxiang and A’xiang ought not to hear, so she asked to speak with Hu privately. “I know where A’qiao has gone—to a convent in Fahua Town. We must lose no time; someone must go for her at once. I think—” She hesitated. “It had better be just Sister A’jin and me. You ought not to meet her.” Hu was utterly bewildered. “What has happened? How do you know where she is? And who is this Sister A’jin?” “There is no time to explain everything now. Little Uncle, just arrange for us to get to Fahua.”

『法华一带都是安庆来的淮军。还不知道好走不好走呢！』『不要紧！』萧家骥说，『我去一趟好了。』『好极！你去最好。』七姑奶奶很高兴地说；因为萧家骥跟淮军首领很熟，此去必定有许多方便。『七姐，我想我还是应该去。』胡雪岩说，『不见面不要紧，至少让她知道我不是不关心她。你看呢？』『我是怕你们见了面吵起来，弄得局面很不好收场。既然小爷叔这么说，去了也不要紧。』到得法华镇，已经黄昏。萧家骥去找淮军大将程家启部下的一个营官，姓朱；人很爽朗热心，问明来意，请他们吃了一顿饭，然后命手下一个把总将地保老胡找了来，说知究竟。

“The whole Fahua district is occupied by Anhui Army troops from Anqing. I do not even know whether we can get through.” “That does not matter,” Xiao said. “I shall go.” “Excellent! You are the best person.” The Seventh Lady was delighted. Xiao knew the Anhui Army commanders well, and his presence would make many things easier. “Seventh Sister, I still think I ought to go,” Hu said. “I need not see her, but at least let her know that I am not indifferent. What do you think?” “I was afraid you would quarrel if you met and make matters impossible to resolve. Since you put it that way, Little Uncle, there is no harm in your going.” It was dusk when they reached Fahua Town. Xiao sought out a battalion commander named Zhu, who served under the Anhui Army general Cheng Xueqi. A frank and helpful man, Zhu heard their errand, gave them a meal, then ordered a subordinate officer, a bazong, to fetch the local constable, Old Hu, and explain what was needed.

『好的，好的！我来领路。』老胡说道∶『请三位跟我来。』于是迎着月色，往东面去；走不多远，折进一条巷子，巷底有处人家，一带粉墙，墙内花木繁盛，新月微光，影影绰绰；薰风过处，传来一阵浓郁的『夜来香』的香味，每个人都觉得精神一振，而一颗心却无缘无故地飘荡不定，有着一种说不出的胀满的感觉。这份感觉以萧家骥为尤甚，不由得便问∶『这是什么地方？』『这里？』地保答道∶『就是白衣庵。晚上来，要走边门。』边门是一道厚实的木板门，举手可及的上方，有个不为人所注意的扁圆形铁环；地保一伸手拉了两下，只听『克啷、克啷』的响声。不久，听得脚步声、然后门开一线，有人问道∶『哪位？』『小音，是我！』『噢！』门内小音问道∶『老胡，这辰光来做啥？』『你有没有看见客人？』地保指着后面的人说，『你跟了尘师父去说，是我带来的人。』

“Certainly, certainly. I shall show the way,” Old Hu said. “The three of you, please follow me.” They headed east in the moonlight and soon turned into a lane. At its far end stood a residence behind a whitewashed wall, with luxuriant flowers and trees inside. In the faint light of the new moon, the shapes were indistinct. A warm breeze carried out the rich scent of night-blooming flowers. Everyone felt suddenly refreshed, yet for no reason their hearts grew restless, filled with a swelling emotion they could not name. Xiao felt it most strongly. “What is this place?” he could not help asking. “Here? White-Robed Convent. At night we use the side entrance.” The side entrance had a solid wooden door. Above it, within reach, was an inconspicuous flattened iron ring. Old Hu reached up and pulled it twice. Clang, clang. After a little while came footsteps; the door opened a crack, and someone asked, “Who is it?” “Xiaoyin, it is me.” “Oh. Old Hu, what brings you here at this hour?” “Can you not see the visitors?” He pointed behind him. “Tell Sister Liaochen that I have brought them.”

门『呀』地一声开了。灯光照处，小音是个俗家打扮的垂发女郎；等客人都进了门，将门关上；然后一言不发地往前走，穿过一条花径，越过两条走廊，到了一处禅房，看样子是待客之处；她停了下去，看着地保老胡。老胡略有些踌躇，『总爷！』他哈腰问∶『是不是我陪着你老在这里坐一坐？』这何消说得？那把总自然照办。于是老胡跟小音悄悄说了几句；然后示意胡雪岩跟着小音走。穿过禅房，便是一个大院子∶绕向西边的回廊，但见人影、花影一齐映在雪白的粉墙上；还有一头猫的影子，弓起背，正在东面屋脊上『叫春』。萧家骥用手肘轻轻将胡雪岩撞了一下，同时口中在念∶『「曲径通幽处，禅房花木深」！』胡雪岩也看出这白衣庵大有蹊跷。但萧家骥的行径，近乎佻亻达；不是礼佛之道，便咳嗽一声，示意他检点。于是默默地随着小音进入另一座院落，一庭树木，三楹精舍，檀香花香，交杂飘送；萧家骥不由得失声赞道∶『好雅致的地方！』『请里面坐。』小音揭开门帘肃客，『我去请了尘师父来。』说完，她又管自己走了。

The door swung open with a creak. By the light they saw Xiaoyin, a girl in ordinary secular dress with her hair hanging loose. Once the visitors were inside, she shut the door and led them forward without a word, along a flower-lined path and through two covered passages to a monastic room apparently used for receiving guests. There she stopped and looked at Old Hu. He hesitated a little, then bowed to the officer. “Sir, shall I keep you company here for a while?” There was scarcely any need to ask; the officer naturally agreed. Old Hu whispered a few words to Xiaoyin, then motioned Hu to follow her. Beyond the room lay a large courtyard. As they turned into the western covered walk, their shadows mingled with those of the flowers upon the whitewashed wall. There was also the shadow of a cat, arching its back and yowling for a mate on the roof to the east. Xiao nudged Hu gently with his elbow and murmured a couplet: “A winding path leads into seclusion; the monks’ quarters lie deep among flowers and trees.” Hu too could see that something about this convent was unusual. But Xiao’s behavior verged on frivolity and was scarcely respectful in a Buddhist sanctuary. He coughed to warn him to restrain himself. They followed Xiaoyin silently into another courtyard, planted with trees and facing an elegant three-bay retreat. Sandalwood incense mingled with the scent of flowers. Xiao exclaimed involuntarily, “What a refined place!” “Please sit inside,” Xiaoyin said, lifting the curtain to admit them. “I shall fetch Sister Liaochen.” Then she went off on her own.

两个人进屋一看，屋中上首供着一座白瓷观音；东面是一排本色的桧木几椅；西面一张极大的木榻，上铺蜀锦棉垫。瓶花吐艳、炉香袅袅，配着一张古琴，布置得精雅非凡；但这一切，都不及悬在木榻上方的一张横披，更使得萧家骥注目。

Entering, the two men saw a white porcelain Guanyin enshrined at the upper end of the room. To the east stood a row of tables and chairs of unpainted cypress; to the west, an enormous wooden couch covered with padded Sichuan brocade. Flowers glowed in vases, incense curled from a burner, and an ancient qin completed an exceptionally tasteful arrangement. Yet none of these things caught Xiao’s attention as much as the horizontal scroll hanging above the couch.

『胡先生！』萧家骥显得有些兴奋，『你看！』横披上是三首诗；胡雪岩总算念得断句∶闲叩禅关访素娥，醮坛药院覆松萝，一庭桂子迎人落，满壁图书献佛多；作赋我应惭宋玉，拈花卿合伴维摩。尘心到此都消尽，细味前缘总是魔！

“Mr Hu!” Xiao sounded excited. “Look!” The scroll contained three poems. Hu could at least make out where the lines began and ended: “At leisure I knock at the Buddhist gate to visit a moonlike beauty; / Pine and creepers cover the ritual altar and the garden of herbs. / A courtyard of osmanthus flowers falls to greet the visitor; / Books and paintings fill the walls, rich offerings to the Buddha. / In writing rhapsodies I must blush before Song Yu; / With a flower in your hand, you should be Vimalakirti’s companion. / Coming here, my worldly thoughts all melt away; / Yet savoring our former ties, I find them all temptation.”

旧传奔月数嫦娥，今叩云房锁丝萝，才调玄机应不让，风怀孙绰扇区我；谁参半分优婆塞？待悟三乘阿笈摩。何日伊蒲同设馔，清凉世界遣诗魔。

“Old legend tells of Chang’e’s flight up to the moon; / Now I knock at a cloudlike cell enclosed in clinging vines. / Your gifts need yield nothing to Xuanji’s; / Your romantic ardor seems greater even than Sun Chuo’s. / Who has attained even half a lay disciple’s practice? / We wait to grasp the Three Vehicles and the Agamas. / When shall we share a Buddhist vegetarian feast, / And in this cool, pure world dispel the demon of verse?”

群花榜上笑良多，梓里云房此日过。君自怜才留好然，我曾击节听高歌；清阴远托伽山竹，冶艳低牵茅屋萝。点缀秋光篱下菊，尽将游思付禅魔。

“On the register of flowers are many traces of smiles; / Today I visit this cloudlike cell in our native place. / Cherishing talent, you have left fine lines behind; / I once beat time in praise as I heard you sing aloud. / Cool shade finds distant shelter in the holy mountain’s bamboo; / Lush beauty trails low among a thatched hut’s vines. / Chrysanthemums beneath the hedge adorn the autumn light; / All wandering thoughts I give to the demon of meditation.”

胡雪岩在文墨这方面，还不及萧家骥，不知道宋玉、孙绰是何许人？也不知道玄机是指的唐朝女道士鱼玄机。佛经上的那些出典是莫名其妙。但诗句中的语气不似对戒律森严的女僧，却是看得出来的。因而愕然相问∶『这是啥名堂？』『你看着好了。』萧家骥轻声答道∶『这位了尘师父，不是嘉兴人就是昆山；不然就是震泽、盛泽。』昆山的尼姑有何异处，胡雪岩不知道；但嘉兴的尼庵是亲自领教过的。震泽和盛泽的风俗，他在吴江同里的时候，也听人说过，这两处地方，盛产丝绸，地方富庶，风俗奢靡。盛泽讲究在尼姑庵宴客，一桌素筵，比燕菜席还要贵；据说是用肥鸡与上好的火腿熬汁调味，所以鲜美绝伦。震泽尼姑庵的烹调，亦是有名的，荤素并行，不逊于无锡的船菜。当然，佳肴以外，还有可餐的秀色。这样回忆着，再又从初见老胡，说夜访白庆庵『没有啥不便』想起，一直到眼前的情景，觉得无一处不是证实了萧家骥的看法，因而好奇大起，渴望着看一看了尘是什么样子？萧家骥反显得比他沉着，『胡先生，』他说，『只怕弄错了！阿巧姐不会在这里。』

In literary matters Hu knew even less than Xiao. He had no idea who Song Yu and Sun Chuo were, nor that Xuanji meant Yu Xuanji, the Tang dynasty Taoist nun. The allusions to Buddhist scriptures were wholly beyond him. Yet he could tell that the tone of the poems was hardly one in which to address a nun who kept strict vows. Astonished, he asked, “What is all this?” “Wait and see,” Xiao answered softly. “This Sister Liaochen must come from Jiaxing or Kunshan. If neither, then Zhenze or Shengze.” Hu knew nothing of what distinguished the nuns of Kunshan, but he had personal experience of the convents of Jiaxing. When staying at Tongli in Wujiang, he had also heard about the customs of Zhenze and Shengze. Both were prosperous silk-producing towns, luxurious in their habits. In Shengze it was fashionable to entertain guests at convents, where a vegetarian banquet cost more than a feast featuring bird’s nest. The dishes were said to be flavored with stock made from plump chickens and the finest ham, which accounted for their extraordinary savor. The convents of Zhenze were equally famous for their cooking: meat and vegetarian dishes alike rivaled the celebrated boat cuisine of Wuxi. Besides the delicacies on the table, of course, there were beauties to feast one’s eyes upon. Remembering all this, Hu thought back to Old Hu’s assurance when they first met that there was “no inconvenience” in visiting White-Robed Convent at night. Everything from that moment to the scene before him seemed to confirm Xiao’s view. His curiosity rose, and he longed to see what Liaochen looked like. Xiao, however, had grown more sober than he. “Mr Hu, I am afraid there has been a mistake. A’qiao cannot be here.”

『何以见得？』『这里，哪是祝发修行的地方？』胡雪岩正待答话，一眼瞥见玻璃窗外，一盏白纱灯笼冉冉而来，便住口不言，同时起身等候；门帘启处，先见小音，次见了尘一若非预知，不会相信所见的是个出家人。她当然也不是纯俗家打扮，不曾『三绺梳头，两截穿衣』发长齐肩，穿的是一件圆领长袍；说它是僧袍固然可以，但僧袍不会用那种闪闪生光的玄色软缎来做，更不会窄腰小袖，裁剪得那么称体。看到脸上，更不象出家人，虽未敷粉，却曾施朱；她的皮肤本来就白，亦无须敷粉。特别是那双眼睛，初看是剪水双瞳，再看才知别蕴春情。

“Why do you say that?” “Is this a place for shaving one’s head and practicing religion?” Hu was about to reply when he glimpsed a white gauze lantern floating toward them beyond the glass window. He fell silent and rose to wait. The curtain lifted; first came Xiaoyin, then Liaochen. Had they not known beforehand, they would never have believed her to be a nun. Her appearance was not entirely secular, certainly. She wore neither an ordinary woman’s three-part coiffure nor separate upper and lower garments. Her hair reached her shoulders, and she had on a long, round-necked robe. One might have called it a nun’s robe, but a nun’s robe would hardly be made of such glossy soft black satin, still less be cut so closely to the body, with a narrow waist and slender sleeves. Her face looked less monastic still. Though she wore no powder, she had applied rouge; her naturally fair skin needed no powder. Above all there were her eyes: at first glance clear as water, but at a second revealing an undertone of amorous feeling.

是这样的人物，便不宜过于持重拘谨，胡雪岩笑嘻嘻地双掌合十，打个问讯∶『可是了尘师太？』『我是了尘。施主尊姓？』『我姑胡。这位姓萧。』于是了尘——行礼，请『施主』落座；她自己盘腿坐在水榻上相陪，动问来意。『原是来见当家老师太的；听地保老胡说，宝庵其实是由了尘师太当家。有点小事打听，请我这位萧老弟说吧！』萧家骥点点头，不谈来意却先问道∶『听了尘师太的口音是震泽？』了尘脸上一红∶『是的。』

With such a person, excessive solemnity and reserve seemed unnecessary. Smiling, Hu brought his palms together in greeting. “Are you Sister Liaochen?” “I am Liaochen. May I ask your surname, benefactor?” “Mine is Hu. This gentleman is Mr Xiao.” Liaochen greeted them in turn and invited her “benefactors” to sit. She herself sat cross-legged on the wooden couch and asked what had brought them. “We originally came to see the elderly abbess,” Hu said. “But Old Hu, the constable, tells us that you are really in charge here. There is a small matter we wish to ask about. Perhaps my young friend Xiao had better explain.” Xiao nodded. Instead of coming to the point, however, he first asked, “Judging by your accent, Sister Liaochen, are you from Zhenze?” She blushed. “Yes.”

『这三首诗，』萧家骥向她上方一指，『好得很！』『也是三位施主，一时雅兴；疯言疯语的，无奈他何！』说着，了尘微微笑了，『萧施主在震泽住过？』『是的。住过一年多；那时还是小孩子，什么都不懂。』『意思是现在都懂了？』这样率直反问，有些咄咄逼人的意味；萧家骥自非弱者，不会艰于应付，从容自若地答道∶『也还不十分懂，改日再来领教。今天有件事，要请了尘师太务必帮个忙。』『言重！请吩咐，只怕帮不了什么忙。『』只要肯帮忙，只是一句话的事『。萧家骥问道∶』白衣庵今天可有一位堂客；是来求当家老师太收容的。这位堂客是闹家务一时想不开，或许她跟当家师太说过，为她瞒一瞒行迹。倘或如此，她就害了白衣庵了！『了尘颜色一变，是受惊的神气；望望这个，又望望那个，终于点点头说∶』有的。可就是这位胡施主的宝眷？『

“These three poems,” Xiao said, pointing above her, “are very fine.” “They were written by three benefactors in moments of poetic inspiration. Such wild nonsense! What can one do with them?” Liaochen smiled faintly. “Have you lived in Zhenze, Mr Xiao?” “Yes, for more than a year. But I was only a child then and understood nothing.” “Meaning that you understand everything now?” So direct a question had something challenging about it. Xiao was no weak opponent and had no difficulty answering with composure. “Not everything, even now. I shall return another day for instruction. Today there is something in which I must ask your help.” “You put it too strongly. Please tell me what you wish. I only fear there may be little I can do.” “If you are willing, a word is all it will take. Has a lady come to White-Robed Convent today to ask the elderly abbess for refuge? She has had domestic difficulties and, in a moment of distress, could see no way out. She may have asked the abbess to conceal her whereabouts. If so, she has done your convent a disservice.” Liaochen’s expression changed; she looked frightened. She glanced from one man to the other, then finally nodded. “Yes, someone has come. Is she perhaps Mr Hu’s lady?”

果然在这里，一旦证实了全力所追求的消息，反倒不知所措。萧家骤与胡雪岩对望着、沉默着；交换的眼色中，提出了同样的疑问∶阿巧姐投身在这白衣庵中，到底是为了什么？若说为了修行，诚如萧家骥所说∶『这里，哪是祝发修行的地方？』倘使不是为了修行，那末非杨即墨，阿巧姐便是另一个了尘。这一层不先弄明白，不能有所决定；这一层要弄明白，却又不知如何着手。终于是胡雪岩作了一个决定∶『了尘师太，我请这位萧老弟先跟敝眷见一面。不知道行不行？』『有什么不行？这样最好。不过，我得先问一问她。』由于了尘赞成萧家骥跟阿巧姐见面，因而可以猜想得到，所谓『问一问她』，其实是劝一劝她。反正只要了尘肯帮忙，一定能够见得着面，胡雪岩和萧家骥就都无话说，愿意静等。等了尘一走，萧家骥问道∶『胡先生，见了阿巧姐，我怎么说？』

So she was here after all. Once the news they had sought so eagerly was confirmed, the two men found themselves at a loss. Xiao and Hu looked at one another in silence, their glances asking the same question: what had A’qiao meant by coming to this convent? If she sought religious discipline, Xiao’s question was justified: “Is this a place for shaving one’s head and practicing religion?” If she did not seek that, she must be choosing the other path and becoming another Liaochen. Until they understood which it was, they could decide nothing; yet they did not know how to begin finding out. At last Hu made a decision. “Sister Liaochen, I should like my young friend Xiao to see my lady first. Would that be possible?” “Why not? That would be best. But I must ask her first.” Since Liaochen approved of Xiao’s seeing A’qiao, they could guess that “asking her” really meant persuading her. Provided Liaochen would help, the meeting was assured. Hu and Xiao said no more and were content to wait. As soon as she had gone, Xiao asked, “Mr Hu, what shall I say when I see A’qiao?”

『我只奇怪，』胡雪岩答非所问∶『这里是怎样一处地方，莫非那个什么阿金一点都不晓得？』『现在没有功夫去追究这个疑问。胡先生，你只说我见了阿巧姐该怎么样？』『什么都不必说，只问问她，到底作何打算？问清楚了，回去跟你师娘商量。』跟阿巧姐见面的地方，是当家老师太养静的那座院子；陈设比不上了尘的屋子，但亦比其他的尼姑庵来得精致，见得白衣庵相当富庶，如果不是有大笔不动产，可以按期坐收租息，便是有丰富的香金收入。

“What puzzles me,” Hu said, without answering, “is whether that woman A’jin knows nothing of the kind of place this is.” “There is no time to investigate that now. Just tell me what I ought to do when I see A’qiao.” “You need say nothing else. Only ask what she means to do. Once you know, we can go back and discuss it with your master’s wife.” Xiao met A’qiao in the courtyard where the elderly abbess lived in quiet retirement. Its furnishings were less fine than those in Liaochen’s rooms, but still more elegant than those of other convents. Plainly White-Robed Convent was prosperous. Either it owned extensive property from which it received regular rents, or its income from devotees’ offerings was substantial.

阿巧姐容颜憔悴，见了萧家骥眼圈都红了；招呼过后，她开门见山地问∶『阿巧姐，你怎么想了想，跑到这地方来了？』『我老早想来了。做人无味，修修来世。』这是说，她的本意是要出家；萧家骤便问∶『这里你以前来过没有？』『没有。』怕隔墙有耳，萧家骥话不能明说；想了一下，记起胡雪岩的疑问，随即问道∶『阿金呢？她来过没有？』这意思是问，阿金如果来过，当然知道这里的情形，莫非不曾跟你说过？『阿巧姐摇摇头∶』也没有。『』那就难怪了！『话只能说这一句；而阿巧姐似乎是了解的，幽幽地叹了口无声的气，仿佛也是有好些话无法畅所欲言似的。

A’qiao looked worn and haggard, and her eyes reddened at the sight of Xiao. After greeting her, he came straight to the point. “A’qiao, whatever made you come to this place?” “I have wanted to come for a long time. Life has no savor. I might as well cultivate merit for the next.” So she had intended to become a nun. Xiao asked, “Have you been here before?” “No.” Afraid of listeners beyond the wall, he could not speak openly. After a moment’s thought he remembered Hu’s question. “What about A’jin? Has she been here?” He meant that, if A’jin had visited, she must know what went on here: had she not told A’qiao? A’qiao shook her head. “No, she has not either.” “That explains it.” He could say no more. A’qiao seemed to understand. She gave a long, soundless sigh, as though she too had much that she could not freely express.

『现在怎么样呢？』萧家骥问道∶『你总有个打算。』『我——，』阿巧姐说，『我先住在这里。慢慢打算。』『也好。』萧家骥说，『明天，我师娘会来看你。』『不要！』阿巧姐断然决然地说∶『请她不要来。』这很奇怪！能见一个象自己这样渊源不深的男客，倒不愿见和向交好的七姑奶奶，而且语气决绝，其中必有缘故。他的思路很快，想得既宽且深；所以在这些地方，格外谨慎，想了一下说∶『阿巧且，我晓得你跟我师娘、感情一向很好；你这话，我回去是不是照实说？』『为什么不能照实说？』

“What now?” Xiao asked. “You must have some plan.” “I—” A’qiao paused. “I shall stay here for the present and decide in time.” “Very well. My master’s wife will come to see you tomorrow.” “No!” A’qiao answered decisively. “Please tell her not to come.” That was extraordinary. She would receive a male visitor with whom she had no particularly close connection, yet refused to see the Seventh Lady, who had long been her friend. Such an emphatic refusal must have a reason. Xiao thought quickly, widely, and deeply; in matters of this kind he was especially cautious. After considering, he said, “A’qiao, I know you have always been very close to my master’s wife. Am I to repeat exactly what you have said?” “Why should you not?”

『那末，我师娘问我∶为啥她不要我去？我怎么答复她？』问到这话，阿巧姐脸上出现了一种怨恨的表情∶『我俗家的亲戚朋友都断了！』她说，『所以不要她来看我；来了我也不见。』语气越发决绝，加上她那种脸色，竟似跟七姑奶奶有不解之仇。萧家骥大为惊骇；可是说话却更谨慎了。『阿巧姐，』他旁敲侧击地探索真相∶『我不也俗家人吗？』这一问算是捉住她话中一个无法辩解的漏洞。她脸上阴晴不定地好半天，终于有了答复∶『萧少爷，说实话，我是怕你师娘。她手段厉害；我弄不过她。再说句实话，做人无味，教人灰心，也就是为了这一点；自以为是心换心的好朋友，哪知道两面三刀，帮着别人来算计我。真正心都凉透了！萧少爷，这话你一定奇怪，一定不相信；行过，你也要想想，我三十多岁的人，各种各样的世面也见识过，总还不致于连人好人坏都看不出，无缘无故冤枉你师娘。你师娘啊，真正是——。』她摇摇头，不肯再说下去。这番话，在萧家骥简直是震动了！他实在不明白，也不能接受她对七姑奶奶这样严酷的批评，楞了好一会才说∶『阿巧姐到底为了啥？我实在想不通！请你说给我听听看。如果是师娘不对，我们做晚辈的，当然不敢说什么；不过肚子里的是非是有的。』『如果，萧少爷，你肯当着菩萨起誓，什么话只摆在肚子里；我就说给你听。』

“Then if she asks why you do not want her to come, what am I to tell her?” At this question a look of resentment came over A’qiao’s face. “I have broken with all my worldly relations and friends. That is why I do not want her here. If she comes, I shall refuse to see her.” Her voice was more determined than ever; coupled with her expression, it suggested an irreconcilable hatred of the Seventh Lady. Xiao was deeply alarmed, but spoke all the more cautiously. “A’qiao,” he asked indirectly, probing for the truth, “am I not a person of the world too?” This exposed a flaw in her argument that she could not explain away. Her expression changed back and forth for a long time before she answered. “Young Master Xiao, to tell the truth, I am afraid of your master’s wife. Her methods are formidable; I am no match for her. And to tell you another truth, this is precisely what has made life seem so empty and disheartening. I thought she was a friend who gave her heart for mine. Who could have known she was two-faced, helping others scheme against me? My heart has turned completely cold. You must find this strange; you must refuse to believe it. But think: I am a woman in my thirties and have seen every sort of thing in the world. Surely I am not so foolish that I cannot tell a good person from a bad one, or would accuse your master’s wife without reason. She is really—” A’qiao shook her head and would say no more. Xiao was shaken to the core. He could neither understand nor accept so harsh a judgment of the Seventh Lady. For a long while he sat stunned. At last he said, “A’qiao, what is this all about? I truly cannot understand. Please tell me. If my master’s wife is in the wrong, those of us of the younger generation would naturally not presume to criticize her. But we know right from wrong in our hearts.” “Young Master Xiao, if you will swear before the Bodhisattva to keep everything I say to yourself, I shall tell you.”

『你是说，你的话不能告诉我师父，师娘？』『对了。』『好！我起誓∶如果阿巧姐对我说的话，我告诉了我师父师娘，叫我天打雷劈。』阿巧姐点头表示满意；然后说道∶『你师娘真叫「又做师娘又做鬼」——。』用这句苟刻的批评开头，阿巧且将七姑奶奶几次劝她的话『夹叙夹议』地从头细诉，照她的看法，完全是七姑奶奶有意要拆散她跟胡雪岩的姻缘，七姑奶奶劝她委屈，入门见礼正正式式做胡家的偏房，看似好意，其实是虚情，因为明知也决不愿这么做，就尽不妨这么说，好逼得不能不下堂求去。

“You mean I must not tell my master or his wife what you say?” “Exactly.” “Very well, I swear it: if I tell either of them what A’qiao tells me, may Heaven strike me dead with lightning.” A’qiao nodded, satisfied. “Your master’s wife really does play both the spirit-medium and the ghost—” Beginning with this harsh judgment, she recounted in detail the several occasions on which the Seventh Lady had advised her, interweaving the conversations with comments of her own. In her view, the Seventh Lady had deliberately set out to break her bond with Hu. Her advice that A’qiao swallow her pride, enter the household, make the proper obeisances, and formally become Hu’s concubine only appeared well meant. It was false kindness. Knowing perfectly well that A’qiao would never agree, she could safely urge it upon her and thereby force her to ask to leave.

对胡雪岩，七姑奶奶在她面前一再说他『滑头』，『没常性，见一个爱一个』；听来是骂胡雪岩而其实是帮他。『萧少爷你想，你这位师娘开口「小爷叔」，闭口』小爷叔『，敬得他来象菩萨。就算他真的「滑头」、「没常性」，又怎好去说他？』阿巧姐说到这里很激动了，「我先倒也当她生来爽直，真的是为我抱不平，所以有啥说啥。后来越想越不对，前前后后，想了又想，才晓得她的意思，无非说胡某人怎么样不是人，犯不着再跟他而已！『听她对七姑奶奶的指责，实在不无道理。但越觉得她有道理，越觉得心里难过；因为萧家骥对他的这位师娘，有如幼弟之于长姐，既敬且爱。多少年来存在心目中的一个伉爽、正直、热心、慷慨的完美印象，此时似乎发现了裂良，怎不教人痛心？因此，他竟没有一句话说。这一方面是感到对阿巧姐安慰，或为七姑奶奶辩护都不甚合适；另一方面也实在是沮丧得什么话都懒得说了。

As for Hu, the Seventh Lady had repeatedly called him “slippery,” a man with “no constancy, who falls in love with every woman he sees.” It sounded like abuse of Hu, but in fact it helped him. “Think, Young Master Xiao. Your master’s wife is forever saying ‘Little Uncle’ this and ‘Little Uncle’ that. She reveres him as though he were a bodhisattva. Even if he really were slippery and inconstant, how could she speak of him that way?” A’qiao had grown agitated. “At first I thought she was naturally outspoken and was truly indignant on my behalf, so she said whatever came into her head. Later, the more I thought, the less it seemed right. I went over everything again and again until I understood. All she meant was that Hu was such a scoundrel that he was not worth staying with!” Her accusations against the Seventh Lady were not without reason. Yet the more reasonable they seemed, the more painful Xiao found them. He regarded his master’s wife as a young brother regards an elder sister, with both respect and affection. For years he had cherished a perfect image of her as forthright, honest, warmhearted, and generous. Now he seemed to see a crack in it. How could that not hurt? He could not utter a word. Neither comforting A’qiao nor defending the Seventh Lady seemed quite appropriate; besides, he was too dejected to feel like saying anything at all.

一见萧家骥的脸色，胡雪岩吓一大跳；他倒象害了一场病似的。何以跟阿巧姐见了一次，有这样的似乎受了极大刺激的神情？令人惊疑莫释，而又苦于不便深问；只问得一句∶『见过面了？』『见过了。我们谢谢了尘师太，告辞吧！』了尘又变得很沉着了，她也不提阿巧姐，只殷勤地请胡雪岩与萧家骥再来『随喜』。居姑庵中何以请男施主来随喜？这话听来便令人有异样之感；只是无暇去分辨她的言外之意。

The sight of Xiao’s face gave Hu a shock. He looked as though he had been ill. What could one meeting with A’qiao have done to leave him so visibly shaken? Hu was troubled and bewildered, yet could hardly question him closely here. He merely asked, “Have you seen her?” “Yes. Let us thank Sister Liaochen and take our leave.” Liaochen had recovered her composure. She too said nothing of A’qiao, only warmly invited the two men to return and “share in the religious joys” of the place. Why should men be invited to enjoy religious visits to a convent? The words had an odd sound, but there was no time to consider what lay beneath them.

不过，胡雪岩对人情应酬上的过节，一向不会忽略，想到有件事该做，随即说了出来∶『请问，缘簿在哪里？』『不必客气了！』胡雪岩已经发现，黄色封面的缘簿，就挂在墙壁上，便随手摘下，文给萧家骥说∶『请你写一写，写一百两银子。』『太多了！』了尘接口说道∶「如果说是为了宝眷住在我们这里，要写这么多，那也用不着！出家人受十方供养，也供养十方；不必胡施主费心。『』那是两回事。『萧家骥越出他的范围，代为回答∶』各人尽各人的心意。『接着，萧家骥便用现成的笔砚，写了缘簿；胡雪岩取一张一百两的银两，夹在缘簿中一起放在桌上，随即告辞出庵。回营谢过朱管带，仍旧由原来护送的人送回上海。一路奔驰，无暇交谈，到了闹区，萧家骥才勒住马说道∶『胡先生，到你府上去细谈。』

Hu, however, never neglected the niceties of social dealings. Remembering something he ought to do, he asked at once, “Where is the book of donations?” “There is no need for such ceremony.” He had already spotted the yellow-covered book hanging on the wall. Taking it down, he handed it to Xiao. “Please enter a hundred taels for me.” “That is too much!” Liaochen interposed. “If you mean to give so much because your lady is staying here, there is no need. Those who have left the world receive support from all quarters and offer support to all quarters. You need not concern yourself.” “Those are separate matters,” Xiao replied on Hu’s behalf, going beyond his own role. “Each of us does what is in his heart.” He used the brush and ink already laid out to make the entry. Hu put a banknote for a hundred taels inside the book, placed it on the table, and took his leave. They returned to the camp to thank Commander Zhu, then rode back to Shanghai under the same escort. They traveled too fast for conversation. Only when they reached the busy streets did Xiao rein in his horse. “Mr Hu, let us go to your house and talk at length.”

于是遣走了那名马弁，一起到胡雪岩与阿巧姐双栖之处。粉奁犹香，明镜如昨；但却别有一股凄凉的意味；胡雪岩换了一个地方，在他书房中闭门深浅。听萧家骥转述了阿巧姐的愤慨之词，胡雪岩才知道他为何有那样的痛苦的神态。当然，在胡雪岩也很难过；自他认识七姑奶奶以来，从未听见有人对她有这样严苛的批评，如今为了自己，使她在阿巧姐口中落了个阴险小人的名声，想想实在对不起七姑奶奶。『胡先生，』萧家骥将一路上不断在想的一句话，问了出来∶『我师娘是不是真的象阿巧姐所说的那样，是有意耍手段？』『是的。』胡雪岩点点头，『这是她过于热心之故。阿巧姐的话，大致都对；只有一点她弄错了。你师娘这样做，实实在在是为她打算。』接着胡雪岩便为七姑奶奶解释，她是真正替阿巧姐的终身打算，既然不愿做偏房，不如分手，择人而事。他虽不知道七姑奶奶有意为阿巧姐与张郎中撮合，但他相信，以七姑奶奶的热心待人，一定会替阿巧姐觅个妥当的归宿。

They dismissed the mounted orderly and went together to the house Hu had shared with A’qiao. Her powder box still held its fragrance; the bright mirror stood as before. Yet the rooms had taken on a desolate air. Hu chose another room, shutting himself in his study with Xiao for a private conversation. When Xiao repeated A’qiao’s indignant words, Hu understood why he had looked so distressed. He too was deeply troubled. In all the time he had known the Seventh Lady, he had never heard anyone criticize her so harshly. Now, because of him, A’qiao had branded her a treacherous schemer. He felt he had done the Seventh Lady a great wrong. “Mr Hu,” Xiao asked, voicing a question that had occupied him all the way back, “has my master’s wife really been deliberately maneuvering things as A’qiao says?” “Yes.” Hu nodded. “She is too eager to help. Most of what A’qiao says is true. She has misunderstood only one point: your master’s wife is doing it entirely for her sake.” He went on to explain. The Seventh Lady was sincerely considering A’qiao’s lifelong welfare. Since she would not become a concubine, she would do better to part from him and choose another man. Hu did not know that the Seventh Lady intended to match her with Dr Zhang, but he believed that, with her warm concern for others, she would certainly find A’qiao a suitable home.

这番解释，萧家骥完全能够接受；甚至可以说，他所希望的，就是这样一番能为七姑奶奶洗刷恶名的解释。因此神态顿时不同；轻快欣慰，仿佛卸下了肩上的重担似的。『原说呢，我师娘怎么会做这种事？她如果听说阿巧姐是这样深的误会，不知道要气成什么样子？』『对了！』胡雪岩矍然惊觉∶『阿巧姐的话，绝对不能跟她说。』『不说又怎么交代？』于是两个人商量如何搪塞七姑奶奶？说没有找到，她会再托阿金去找；说是已经祝发，决不肯再回家，她一定亦不会死心，自己找到白衣庵去碰钉子。想来想去没有妥当的办法。

Xiao could accept this explanation completely. Indeed, it was precisely what he had hoped for: an explanation that would clear the Seventh Lady of the charge against her. His manner changed at once. He became cheerful and relieved, as though a heavy burden had slipped from his shoulders. “That is what I thought! How could my master’s wife do such a thing? If she heard how deeply A’qiao misunderstood her, there is no knowing how angry she would be.” “Exactly!” Hu suddenly took alarm. “You must on no account tell her what A’qiao said.” “But if we say nothing, how are we to explain?” They discussed how to put the Seventh Lady off. If they said they had not found A’qiao, she would ask A’jin to look again. If they said A’qiao had shaved her head and absolutely refused to return, she would still persist and go to White-Robed Convent herself, only to be rebuffed. However much they thought, they could find no satisfactory answer.

丢下这层不谈，萧家骥问道∶『胡先生，那末你对阿巧姐，究竟作何打算呢？』这话也使得胡雪岩很难回答；心里转了好半天的念头，付之一叹∶『我只有挨骂了！』『这是说，决定割舍？』『不割舍又如何？』『那就这样，索性置之不理。』萧家骥说∶『心肠要硬就硬到底！』『是我自己良心上的事。』胡雪岩说，『置之不理，似乎也不是办法。』『怎么才是办法？』萧家骥说，『要阿巧姐心甘情愿地分手，是办不到的事。』

Leaving that difficulty aside, Xiao asked, “Mr Hu, what do you mean to do about A’qiao?” That too was hard for Hu to answer. He turned it over in his mind for a long time, then sighed. “I can only resign myself to being cursed.” “You mean you have decided to give her up?” “What else can I do?” “Then leave the matter entirely alone,” Xiao said. “If you are to harden your heart, harden it all the way.” “It is a matter of my own conscience,” Hu replied. “Ignoring her altogether hardly seems right.” “What would be right, then? There is no way to make A’qiao agree willingly to the separation.”

『不求她心甘情愿，只望她咽得下那口气。』胡雪岩作了决定∶『我想这样子办——。』他的办法是一方面用缓兵之计，隐住七姑奶奶，只说阿巧姐由白衣庵的当家师太介绍，已远赴他乡，目前正派人追下去劝驾了；一方面要拜托怡情老二转托阿金∶第一、帮着瞒谎，不能在七姑奶奶面前道破真相；第二、请她跟阿巧姐去见一面，转达一句话，不管阿巧姐要干什么，祝发也好，从良也好，乃至于步了尘的后尘也好，胡雪岩都不会干预，而且预备送她一大笔钱。说完了他的打算，胡雪岩自己亦有如释重负之感；因为牵缠多日，终于有了快刀斩乱麻的处置。而在萧家骥，虽并不以为这是一个好办法；只是除此以外，别无善策，而况毕竟事不干己，要想使劲出力也用不上，只有点点头表示赞成。『事不宜迟，你师娘还在等回音；该干什么干什么，今天晚上还要辛苦你。』『胡先生的事就等于我师父的事，』萧家骥想了一下说，『我们先去看怡情老二。』

“I do not ask for willing agreement. I only hope she can swallow the bitterness.” Hu made his decision. “This is what I propose—” He would first gain time and keep the Seventh Lady quiet by saying that the abbess of White-Robed Convent had sent A’qiao to another place far away, and that someone was already following to persuade her to return. At the same time, he would ask the Second Miss to enlist A’jin’s help. First, A’jin must support the story and never reveal the truth to the Seventh Lady. Second, she must see A’qiao and deliver a message: whatever A’qiao wished to do—take the tonsure, marry respectably, or even follow in Liaochen’s footsteps—Hu would not interfere. He was also ready to give her a large sum of money. Once he had explained the plan, Hu too felt relieved. After so many days of entanglement, he had at last found a way to cut through it. Xiao did not consider it a good solution, but could think of no better one. Besides, it was not his own affair; however much he wished to help, there was little he could do. He could only nod his agreement. “We must act at once,” Hu said. “Your master’s wife is still waiting for news. Let us do what needs doing. I must trouble you with more work tonight.” “Your business is as much my concern as my master’s.” Xiao thought for a moment. “Let us see the Second Miss first.”

到了怡情老二那里，灯红酒绿，夜正未央。不过她是『本家』，另有自己的『小房子』；好在相去不远，『相帮』领着，片刻就到。入门之时，正听得客厅里的自鸣钟打十二下；怡情老二虽不曾睡，却已上楼回卧室了。听得小大姐一报，她请客人上楼。端午将近的天气，相当闷热；她穿一件家常绸夹袄对客，袖管很大也很短，露出两弯雪白的膀子，一只手膀上戴一支金镯，一只手腕上戴一支翠镯，丰容盛髻、一副福相；这使得萧家骥又生感触，相形之下，越觉得阿巧姐憔悴可怜。由于胡、萧十分是初次光临，怡情老二少不得有一番周旋，倒茶摆果碟子，还要『开灯』请客人『躺一息』。主要殷勤，客人当然也要故作闲豫，先说些不相干的话，然后谈入正题。

At the Second Miss’s establishment, lamps glowed red, wine flowed, and the night was still young. But she was the proprietress and had a separate little house of her own. Fortunately it was nearby; an attendant led them there in a few moments. As they entered, they heard the clock in the sitting room strike twelve. The Second Miss had not gone to sleep, though she had retired upstairs to her bedroom. When her maid announced the visitors, she invited them up. With the Dragon Boat Festival approaching, the weather had grown close and hot. She received them in an informal lined silk jacket whose broad, short sleeves exposed her white forearms. On one arm she wore a gold bracelet, on the other a jade bangle. Her full face and abundant, carefully dressed hair gave her a look of prosperity and good fortune. The sight stirred Xiao again: by comparison, A’qiao seemed all the more worn and pitiable. Since this was the two men’s first visit to her house, the Second Miss had to observe the usual courtesies. She poured tea, set out dishes of fruit, and even offered to light the opium lamp and let them recline for a while. Before such hospitality, the guests too had to make a show of being at leisure. They began with irrelevant conversation before turning to their purpose.

萧家骥刚说得一句『阿巧姐果然在白衣庵』，小大姐端着托盘进房；于是小酌宵夜，一面继谈此行经过。萧家骥话完；胡雪岩接着开口，拜托怡情老二从中斡旋。一直静听不语的怡情老二，不即置答；事情太离奇了，她竟一时摸不清头绪。眨着眼想了好一会才摇摇头说∶『胡老爷，我看事情不是这么做法。这件事少不得七姑奶奶！』接着，她谈到张郎中；认为七姑奶奶的做法是正办。至于阿巧姐有所误会，无论如何是解释得清楚的。为今之计，只有设法将阿巧姐劝了回来；化解误会，消除怨恨，归嫁张宅，这一切只要大家同心协心花功夫下去，一定可以有圆满的结局。『阿金不必让她插手了；决绝的话，更不可以说。现在阿巧姐的心思想偏了，要耐心拿它慢慢扭过来。七姑奶奶脾气虽毛糙，倒是最肯体恤人、最肯顾大局；阿巧姐的误会，她肯原谅的，也肯委屈的。不过话可以跟她说明白；犯不着让她一白衣庵去碰钉了。我看，胡老爷——。』她有意不再说下去，是希望胡雪岩有所意会，自动作一个表示。而胡雪岩的心思很乱，不耐细想，率直问道∶『二阿姐，你要说啥？』

Xiao had barely said, “A’qiao was at White-Robed Convent after all,” when the maid came in with a tray. Over a little wine and a late supper, he continued his account of the visit. When he finished, Hu asked the Second Miss to act as intermediary. She had listened without a word and did not answer at once. The whole affair was so strange that she could scarcely make sense of it. For a while she blinked in thought, then shook her head. “Mr Hu, I do not think that is the way to handle matters. We cannot do without the Seventh Lady in this.” She told him about Dr Zhang and argued that the Seventh Lady’s course was the right one. A’qiao’s misunderstanding could surely be explained away. What they must do now was persuade her to return, clear up the misunderstanding, dispel her resentment, and arrange her marriage into the Zhang household. If everyone worked together patiently, there was every prospect of a happy conclusion. “There is no need to involve A’jin, and you certainly must not send a message that closes every door. A’qiao’s thoughts have taken a wrong turning; we must patiently guide them back. The Seventh Lady may be hasty, but no one is more considerate or more willing to think of everyone’s interests. She will forgive A’qiao’s misunderstanding and put up with some unfairness. We can explain matters to her openly; there is no reason to let her go to the convent and be rebuffed. As I see it, Mr Hu—” She deliberately stopped, hoping that Hu would understand and volunteer the necessary offer. But his mind was in turmoil and he had no patience for subtlety. “What do you mean, Second Sister?”

『我说，胡老爷，你委屈一点，明天再亲自到白衣庵去一趟，陪个笑脸，说两句好话，拿阿巧姐先劝了回来再说。』这个要求，胡雪岩答应不下。三番两次，牵缠不清，以致于搁下好多正事不能办；他心里实在也厌倦了。如今好不容易有了个快刀斩乱麻的措施，却又不能实行；反转要跟阿巧姐去陪笑脸，说好话，不但有些于心不甘，也怕她以为自己回心转意，觉得少不得她，越发牵缠得紧，岂不是更招麻烦？看他面难色，怡情老二颇为着急说∶『胡老爷，』她说∶『别样见识，我万万不及你们做官的老爷们；只有这件事上，我有把握。为啥呢？女人的心思，只有女人晓得；再说，阿巧姐跟我相处也不止一年，她的性情，我当然摸得透。胡老爷，我说的是好话，你不听会懊悔！』胡雪岩本对怡情老二有些成见，觉得她未免有所袒护，再听她这番话，成见自然加深，所以一时并无表示，只作个沉吟的样了，当作不以为然的答复。

“I mean that you should put your pride aside a little. Go to White-Robed Convent again yourself tomorrow, smile, say a few kind words, and first persuade A’qiao to return. We can consider the rest afterward.” Hu could not agree. This repeated and endless entanglement had forced him to neglect a great deal of important business; he was thoroughly weary of it. Now that he had finally found a way to cut himself free, he was to be prevented from using it. Instead, he must smile at A’qiao and speak ingratiatingly. He resented that; worse, he feared she would think he had changed his mind and could not do without her. She would cling to him still more tightly. Would that not merely invite further trouble? Seeing his reluctance, the Second Miss grew anxious. “Mr Hu, in every other kind of judgment I am far below gentlemen in official life such as yourself. But on this matter I am confident. Why? Because only a woman understands a woman’s thoughts. Besides, A’qiao and I lived together for more than a year. Naturally I know her disposition. I am giving you good advice. If you refuse it, you will regret it.” Hu already suspected the Second Miss of being partial to A’qiao, and her words only strengthened his prejudice. He made no commitment, merely adopting a thoughtful expression to indicate his disagreement.

萧家骥旁观者清，一方面觉得怡情老二的话虽说得率直了些，而做法是高明的；另一方面又知道胡雪岩的心境，这时不便固劝，越劝越坏。好在巧姐的下落明了，在白衣庵多住些日子亦不要紧。为了避免造成僵局，只有照『事缓则圆』这句话去做。『胡先生也有胡先生的难处；不过你的宗旨是对的！』他加重了语气，同时对怡情老二使个眼色，『慢慢来，迟早要拿事情办通的。』『也好。请萧少爷劝劝胡老爷！』『我知道，我知道。』萧家骥连声答应，『明天我给你回话。今天不早了，走吧！』

As an onlooker, Xiao could see more clearly. The Second Miss had spoken rather bluntly, but her approach was sound. Yet he also understood Hu’s state of mind: pressing him now would only make things worse. Fortunately, they knew where A’qiao was, and there was no harm in her remaining at the convent a little longer. To avoid a deadlock, they must follow the maxim that matters settle more smoothly when given time. “Mr Hu has his own difficulties. But your intention is right.” Xiao emphasized the words and gave the Second Miss a meaningful look. “Let us take things slowly. Sooner or later we shall find a way through.” “Very well. Please try to persuade him, Young Master Xiao.” “I will, I will,” Xiao promised repeatedly. “I shall bring you an answer tomorrow. It is late now. We should be going.”

辞别出门，胡雪岩步履蹒跚，真有心力交瘁之感。萧家骥当然亦不便多说，只问一句∶『胡先生，你今在歇在哪里？我送你去。』『我到钱庄里去睡。』胡雪岩说道∶『你今天还要不要去见你师娘。』『今天就不必去了。这么晚！』『好的。』。胡雪岩沉吟了一会，皱眉摇头，显得不胜其烦似的，『等一两天再说吧！我真的脑筋都笨了，从来没有见过这种拉拉扯扯，弄不清爽的麻烦！『』那末，『萧家骥低声下气地，倒像自己惹上了麻烦，向人求教那样∶』明天见了我师娘，我应当怎么说？『这一次胡雪岩答得非常爽脆∶』只要不伤你师娘的心，怎么说都可以。『回到钱庄，只为心里懊恼，胡雪岩在床上辗转反侧，直到市声渐起，方始朦胧睡去。

They took their leave. Hu walked unsteadily, utterly exhausted in body and mind. Xiao could hardly add anything; he only asked, “Where will you sleep tonight, Mr Hu?
