He wanted a definite plan, so that he could grasp Zuo’s intention and help carry it out. He therefore asked, “Then does Your Excellency find something useful in my humble opinion?” “Humble opinion? Your judgment is excellent!” Zuo paused thoughtfully. “Still, I am not a man to change my face at a turn of the hand. Besides, Li Shaoquan has always been, to me—” He too left the sentence unfinished. Anyone familiar with his usual remarks could supply the rest: he had always despised Li Hongzhang. To seek friendship now seemed like asking a favor, and he resented it. Hu decided that open advice toward a proper end was different from privately criticizing others. Even if such words leaked out, they could stand in public without injuring his reputation. He resolved to persuade Zuo to cooperate with Li.

『大人，』他有意问道∶『如今唯一的急务是什么？』『你是指公事，还是指我自己的事？』『公事也是如此，大人的私事也是如此。一而二，二而一，无大不大的一件大事是什么？』『自在是肃清全浙。』『是，肃清全浙只剩一处障碍；就是湖州。拿湖州攻了下来，就可奏报肃清。那时候，大人也要封侯拜相了。』『拜相还早，封侯亦不足为奇。果然膺此分茅之赏，我是要力辞的。』胡雪岩不知道他这话是有感而发，还是故作矫情，反正不必与他争辩，惟有顺着他的语气想话来说，才能打动他的心。

“My lord,” he asked deliberately, “what is the one urgent task before us?” “Do you mean public business, or my own affairs?” “It is the same in both. Two matters in one, and one in two: what is the great task that concerns both?” “Naturally, to clear all Zhejiang of rebels.” “Exactly. And there is only one obstacle left: Huzhou. Once it falls, you can report the province pacified. Then you too will be made a marquis and a grand minister.” “A grand minister is far in the future, and a marquisate is nothing remarkable. If such a grant of nobility is offered, I shall insist upon declining it.” Hu could not tell whether Zuo spoke from real feeling or affected indifference. There was no point in arguing. Only by following the direction of his words could Hu move him.

『大人这一首高！』他着大拇指说∶『封侯不希罕，见得富贵于我如浮云，比曾相、李中丞都高一等了。不过，朝廷如无恩命，大人又怎能显得出高人一等的人品？』『这话倒也是。』左宗棠深深点头。左宗棠终于松了口，胡雪岩也就松了口气。至于如何与李鸿章 合作？就不用他费心了；一切形势，左宗棠看得很清楚，而且谈用兵，亦不是他所能置喙的。他只提醒左宗棠一点，会攻江宁，李鸿章 忤了朝旨；目前急图补救，所以即使左宗棠不愿与他合作，他自己亦会派兵进窥湖州，表示遵从朝廷所一再揭示的，『疆臣办贼，决不可有轸域之分』的要求。左宗棠亦实在需要李鸿章的支援。

“A masterly move, my lord!” Hu raised his thumb. “To think nothing of a marquisate shows that wealth and rank are no more to you than passing clouds. That places you above both Grand Secretary Zeng and Governor Li. But unless the court first offers the honor, how can you display such superior character?” “There is truth in that.” Zuo nodded deeply. At last he had yielded a little, and Hu could breathe freely. How cooperation with Li was to be arranged no longer required Hu’s attention. Zuo understood the whole situation, and military strategy was not a subject on which Hu could presume to speak. He merely reminded Zuo of one point: Li had disobeyed the court’s orders to assist at Jiangning and now urgently wished to make amends. Even if Zuo refused cooperation, Li would send troops toward Huzhou on his own, demonstrating obedience to the repeatedly stated principle that provincial authorities suppressing rebels must not let territorial boundaries divide their efforts. Zuo, moreover, truly needed his support.

第一是兵力。湖州已成为东南长毛的逋光薮，残兵败将交集结在一起，人数超过左军好几倍。而且逼得急，会作困兽之斗，决不可轻视。第二是地形。湖州四周，港汊纵横，处处可以设仗邀击，本是易守难攻之地；当年赵景贤孤城坚持，因势制宜，将地形的利用，发挥到了极致。如今长毛守湖州的主将黄文金，亦非弱者；且假『幼主』洪福真的名号以行，指挥容易。而且湖州所贮存的粮食，据报可以支持一年，这又比赵景贤当时的处境好得多了。这进取湖州的两大障碍，都不是左宗棠独力所能克服的；而亦惟有李鸿章可以帮助他克服这两大障碍。论兵力，有苏军的协力，才可以完成对湖州的包围——当然不是象曾国荃攻金陵那样的四面包围。如果采取这样的方略，即使兵力部署上能够做得到，亦是不智之举；从古以来，围城往往网开一面，因为不放敌人一条生路，必然作生死的搏斗，就算能够尽歼敌人，自己这方面的伤亡，亦一定是惨重无比。反过来看，留下一个纵敌的缺口，正可以激起敌军的恋生之念，瓦解他的斗志。而况在预先安排好的敌人逃生路上，可以处处设伏，反为得计。

The first reason was manpower. Huzhou had become the refuge of the rebels of the southeast. Their scattered armies and defeated commanders had gathered there in numbers several times greater than Zuo’s forces. Pressed too hard, they would fight like trapped beasts and must not be underestimated. The second reason was terrain. Around Huzhou, waterways branched in every direction, offering ambush positions everywhere. The place was naturally easy to defend and difficult to attack. When Zhao Jingxian had held the isolated city, he had adapted his defense to the ground and used it to the utmost. Its present rebel commander, Huang Wenjin, was no weakling either. Acting in the Young Heavenly King’s name, he could issue orders readily. Reports also said that Huzhou held enough grain for a year, placing him in a much better position than Zhao had enjoyed. Zuo could overcome neither obstacle alone; only Li could help him surmount both. In manpower, the assistance of the Jiangsu forces was needed to complete the investment of Huzhou—not, of course, a four-sided encirclement like Zeng Guoquan’s siege of Jinling. Even if enough troops could be deployed for that, it would be unwise. Since ancient times, besiegers had often left one side open. Give the enemy no way to live, and he must fight to the death. Even if annihilated, he would inflict terrible losses. Leave an outlet, by contrast, and the hope of survival would weaken his will to resist. Moreover, ambushes could be laid along a carefully prepared escape route. That was the better calculation.

论地形，湖州外围的第一要隘是北面出太湖的大钱口；当年赵景贤雪夜失大钱，导致湖州的不守。以今视昔，情势不殊，要破湖州须先夺大钱；而夺大钱，苏军渡太湖南下，比左军迂道而北要方便得多。同时最大的关键是，攻大钱必须要用水师，而这又是左军之所短，苏军之所长。李鸿章 当然要用他之所长，尽力有所作为，既以弥补常州顿兵之咎；亦以无负锡封爵位之恩。左宗棠自与胡雪岩深谈以后，默默打算；自己这方面地利、人和都不及李鸿章 ，如果不能大包大揽，放下诺言，限期独力攻克湖州，就不能禁止李鸿章 驰驱前路，自北面攻湖州。两军不能合作，便成争功的局面；李鸿章 争不过无所谓，自己争不过，让李鸿章 喧宾夺主，那就一世英名付之流水了。他想来想去，因人成事，利用李鸿章 相助，是为上策。自己只要尽到了地主的道理，客军不能不处处情让，即使苏军先攻入湖州，李鸿章 亦总不好意思，径自出奏。只要光复湖州的捷报由自己手中发出，铺叙战功，便可以操纵了。

As for terrain, the first vital position outside Huzhou was Daqiankou, opening northward onto Lake Tai. Zhao Jingxian’s loss of Daqian on a snowy night had led to the fall of the city. The circumstances were much the same now: Huzhou could not be taken until Daqian was seized. It was far easier for the Jiangsu troops to cross Lake Tai from the north than for Zuo’s forces to march around to it. Most importantly, an attack on Daqian required a naval force—the Jiangsu army’s strength and Zuo’s weakness. Li would naturally use that strength to the full, both to atone for remaining idle at Changzhou and to justify his newly bestowed title. After his long talk with Hu, Zuo considered matters quietly. In local advantages and connections, his position was inferior to Li’s. Unless he could undertake the whole task himself and promise to capture Huzhou unaided within a fixed time, he could not prevent Li from advancing against it from the north. Without cooperation, the two armies would compete for glory. If Li lost the contest, little harm was done to him. If Zuo lost and allowed his guest to displace him as host, the reputation of a lifetime would be ruined. After much thought, Zuo decided that the best course was to achieve his purpose with Li’s assistance. If he fulfilled his duties as host, the visiting army would have to show him courtesy at every turn. Even if the Jiangsu troops entered Huzhou first, Li could scarcely send his own independent memorial. Provided the report of victory went through Zuo’s hands, he could control the account of the achievements.

打定了主意，暂且做一个能屈能伸的大丈夫；左宗棠亲自提笔，写了一封极恳切的信给李鸿章 ，在商略扫荡东南余孽的策略中，透露出求援之意。李鸿章 亦很漂亮，答应将他部下的『郭刘潘杨四军』，全数投入湖州战场。郭刘潘杨——郭松林、刘铭传、潘鼎新、杨鼎勋四军，是淮军的中坚；其实李鸿章投入湖州战场，还不止这四军，另有以翰林从军的刘秉璋，与曾国藩小同乡、江南提督黄翼升的水师，亦奉委派，分道助攻。朱鸿章 的心思与左宗棠大致相同，有意大张声势，将进攻湖州一役，看得不下如金陵之复，一方面象押宝似的，希望能俘获『幼逆』，掘得『金穴』；一方面亦是有心扫扫曾军的兴头。

His mind made up, Zuo would for the moment be a great man capable of bending as well as standing firm. He personally wrote Li a most earnest letter, discussing how to sweep away the remaining rebels of the southeast and hinting at his need for assistance. Li responded handsomely, promising to commit all four of his “Guo, Liu, Pan, and Yang armies” to Huzhou. These commands—Guo Songlin’s, Liu Mingchuan’s, Pan Dingxin’s, and Yang Dingxun’s—formed the backbone of the Anhui Army. In fact, Li sent more than those four. Liu Bingzhang, who had joined the army from the Hanlin Academy, was also ordered to assist, as was the naval force of Huang Yisheng, Jiangnan’s provincial military commander and a close fellow townsman of Zeng Guofan. They would advance by different routes. Li’s intentions broadly resembled Zuo’s. He meant to make a great display and treat the Huzhou campaign as scarcely less important than the recovery of Jinling. Like a gambler placing a wager, he hoped to capture the young rebel and uncover a hoard of treasure; at the same time, he wished to dampen the Hunan Army’s elation.

在湖州的长毛，号称二十万，至少亦有六折之数；左李两方，正规军合起来不下八万，加上随军的文员、夫役，总数亦在十万以上。彼此旗鼓相当，发生恶战是意中之事；但胜负已如前定，而且长毛败退的情况，大致亦在估计之中。因为由于地形的限制，进取的方向，只能顺势而行。左宗棠所部由湖州东南、西南两方面进逼；苏军则由东北、西北分攻，并从正北进扼大钱口，以防长毛窜入太湖。湖州的东面，是东南最富庶的地区，有重兵防守，而且东到海滨，并无出路；在湖州的长毛，唯一的出路，只是向西，如能冲过广德，则江西有李世贤、汪海洋，都是长毛中有名的悍将，能会合在一起，或者还有苟延残喘的可能。战场如棋局，不但敌我之间，尔虞我诈；就是联手的一方，亦在钩心斗角——李鸿章 毕竟还是下了一着专为自己打算的棋，将刘铭传的二十营，陆续拔队，指向浙皖之交；名为进攻广德，断贼归路，其实是想拦截黄文金，俘『幼逆』，夺辎重。

The rebels at Huzhou claimed two hundred thousand men and probably had at least sixty percent of that number. Zuo’s and Li’s regular forces together numbered no fewer than eighty thousand; with civilian officials, laborers, and other followers, the total exceeded a hundred thousand. The sides were roughly matched, and fierce fighting was expected. Yet the outcome was virtually predetermined, and even the general course of the rebel retreat could be foreseen. The ground constrained the directions of advance. Zuo’s troops would press from the southeast and southwest, while the Jiangsu forces attacked from northeast and northwest and moved directly south to block Daqiankou, preventing escape onto Lake Tai. East of Huzhou lay the richest country in the southeast, heavily defended; beyond it was the coast, offering no way out. The rebels’ only escape lay westward. If they broke through Guangde, they might join Li Shixian and Wang Haiyang in Jiangxi, both famous fighting commanders, and perhaps prolong their existence a little. A battlefield was like a chessboard. Deception flourished not only between enemies, but among allies competing against one another. Li did, after all, make a move for his own advantage. He sent Liu Mingchuan’s twenty battalions, one after another, toward the Zhejiang–Anhui border, ostensibly to attack Guangde and cut the rebels’ retreat. His real aim was to intercept Huang Wenjin, capture the young ruler, and seize the baggage train.

湖州终于在七月二十六克复了。如事先所估计的，黄文金果然开湖州西门遁走。大队长毛分三路西窜，到了广德，又分两路，一路向皖南；一路是由黄文金带着『幼逆』，由宁国过西天目山，经开化、玉山窜入江西境内。刘铭传穷追不舍；其他各军为了争功，亦无不奋勇当先，连追五日五夜，长毛溃不成军，黄文金死在乱军之中了。但是洪福真却还是下落不明；比较可靠的传说是由江西南下，打算与窜至广东、福建边境的李世贤、汪海洋会合。然后西趋湖北；与『扶王』陈德才联结，自荆襄西入陕西，在关中另起一个局面。这当然是一把如意算盘。但即令打不成功，这样窜来窜去，如与安徽、河南的捻匪合流亦是大可忧之事。因此，朝廷对两次三番，穷追猛打，而竟未能促住『幼逆』，置之于法，深为恼火。更恼火的是左宗棠。『全浙肃清』的折子已经拜发，而洪福真未获，就不能算克竟全功，一时还难望分茅之赏。

Huzhou was finally recovered on the twenty-sixth day of the seventh month. As predicted, Huang opened the western gate and fled. The main rebel forces escaped west in three columns. At Guangde they divided again into two routes: one led into southern Anhui; the other, taken by Huang with the young ruler, went through Ningguo, over the western Tianmu Mountains, and by Kaihua and Yushan into Jiangxi. Liu Mingchuan pursued relentlessly. The other armies, eager for credit, also pressed forward with all their strength. After five days and nights of pursuit, the rebels were scattered beyond cohesion, and Huang died amid the fighting. Hong Tianguifu, however, was still missing. The more credible reports said that he was moving south through Jiangxi to join Li Shixian and Wang Haiyang on the Guangdong–Fujian border. From there they intended to turn west toward Hubei, link up with King Fu, Chen Decai, and pass from the Jingzhou–Xiangyang region into Shaanxi, establishing themselves anew in Guanzhong. This was certainly a hopeful calculation. Yet even if it failed, such ceaseless movement was dangerous: a junction with the Nian rebels of Anhui and Henan would give grave cause for concern. The court was therefore deeply angered that repeated, relentless pursuit had still failed to capture the young rebel and bring him to justice. Zuo was angrier still. His memorial announcing “all Zhejiang cleared of rebels” had already gone forward, but with Hong Tianguifu uncaptured, the achievement remained incomplete. For the time being, he could hardly expect his grant of nobility.

辨明了『十万』之说；再论纠参部下的责任，言语晚为犀利∶『至云杭城全数出窜，未闻纠参，尤不可解。金陵早已合围，而杭州则并未能合围也；金陵报』杀贼净尽『，杭州报「首逆实已窜出」也！』仅是这两句话，便如老吏断狱，判定曾国荃有不容贼众逸出的责任，而曾国藩有谎报军情的罪过。但在结尾上，却又笔锋一转，故弄狡猾∶『臣因军事最尚质实，故不得不辩。至此后公事，均仍和衷商办，臣断不敢稍存意见，自重衍尤。』这段话是所谓『绵里针』，看来戒慎谦和；其实棱角森然，句句暗隐着指责曾国藩的意思在内。

Having disposed of the claim of “a hundred thousand,” Zuo turned to responsibility for impeaching negligent subordinates, and his language grew still sharper: “As for the statement that the entire enemy force escaped from Hangzhou and no impeachments were heard of, this is particularly incomprehensible. Jinling had long been completely surrounded; Hangzhou had not been surrounded at all. From Jinling came the report, ‘All the rebels have been killed.’ From Hangzhou came the report, ‘The principal rebels have indeed escaped.’” Those two sentences alone had the force of an experienced magistrate’s judgment: Zeng Guoquan had been responsible for preventing escape, and Zeng Guofan had falsely reported the military situation. At the close, however, the pen turned again with calculated subtlety. “In military affairs, truth and substance are of the first importance; I have therefore had no choice but to explain. In all future public business I shall continue to consult and cooperate harmoniously. I would not dare harbor the slightest prejudice and thereby increase my own fault.” These were needles wrapped in silk. Cautious and modest on the surface, the words were sharp beneath; every sentence contained a concealed accusation against Zeng Guofan.

这通奏折发出，不过半个月便有了回音。由恭王出面的『廷寄』，措词异常婉转，不说一时还不能封左宗棠的爵，却说『左宗棠自入浙以来，克复城隘数十处，肃清全境，厥功甚伟。本欲即加懋赏，恐该督以洪幼逆未灭，必将固辞；一俟余孽净尽，即降恩旨。』是很明显地暗示，左宗棠封爵，不过迟早间事。关于他与曾国藩的争辩，亦有温愉∶『朝廷有功诸臣，不欲苛求细故。该督于洪幼逆之入浙，则据实入告；于其出境则派兵跟追，均属正办。所称此后公事仍与曾国潘和衷商办，不敢稍存意见，尤得大臣之体。深堪嘉尚。朝廷所望于该督者，至大且远；该督其益加勉励，为一代名臣，以副厚望。』上谕中虽未责备曾国藩，但是非好恶，已表现得很清楚。而许左宗棠以『一代名臣』，更是上谕中难得一见的字样。总之这一场御裁的笔墨官司，左宗棠占尽上风；而与曾国藩的怨，自然也结得更深了。

Within half a month of the memorial’s dispatch, a reply came. Issued through Prince Gong, the confidential court dispatch was extraordinarily tactful. Instead of saying that Zuo could not yet be ennobled, it declared: “Since entering Zhejiang, Zuo Zongtang has recovered dozens of cities and fortified positions and cleared the whole province. His achievement is very great. We had intended at once to bestow a substantial reward, but feared that, with the young rebel Hong still undestroyed, the governor-general would insist upon declining it. As soon as the remaining rebels are eliminated, a decree of favor will be issued.” This clearly implied that Zuo’s ennoblement was only a matter of time. There was gentle reassurance concerning his dispute with Zeng as well. “The court does not wish to press meritorious servants over minor details. When the young rebel Hong entered Zhejiang, the governor-general reported the facts; when he left the province, troops were sent in pursuit. Both were proper actions. His declaration that he will continue to consult harmoniously with Zeng Guofan in public affairs, harboring no prejudice, particularly accords with the bearing of a great minister and deserves high praise. The court’s expectations of him are great and far-reaching. Let him exert himself still further and become an eminent minister of his age, fulfilling our hopes.” The edict did not reproach Zeng, but its judgment of right and wrong was clear. The promise that Zuo might be “an eminent minister of his age” was especially rare language in an imperial decree. In this dispute of memorials, submitted to the sovereign’s judgment, Zuo had gained the advantage on every point. Naturally, his enmity with Zeng deepened as well.

曾左结怨，形诸表面的，是口舌之争；暗中拼命抵拒的，是地盘之争。而又象在夹缝中受挤，又象首当其冲的是曾国荃。曾国荃的本职是浙江巡抚。用失之时，为了鼓励将帅，不按建制任职；此省大员在他省领兵，事所常有。但战事告一段落，情形就不一样了。照常理而论，曾国荃即令破江宁以后有过失，到底百战功高；应该让他赴浙江巡抚本任，才是正办。无奈左宗棠以闽浙总督兼署浙巡，绝无退让之意。而曾国藩为曾国荃告病，虽由于忧谗畏讥，以急流勇退作明哲保身之计；其实亦是看透了老弟有『妾身不分明』的隐衷，估量他决不能到任，不如自己知趣。

On the surface, the quarrel between Zeng and Zuo was a war of words; beneath it lay a fierce struggle for territory. Caught between them, and at the same time bearing the first impact, was Zeng Guoquan. His substantive appointment was Governor of Zhejiang. In wartime, to encourage commanders, appointments had not followed ordinary administrative boundaries. A senior official of one province leading troops in another was nothing unusual. Once a phase of the war ended, however, the situation changed. By ordinary reasoning, whatever faults Zeng Guoquan might have committed after taking Jiangning, his distinction in a hundred battles was undeniable. The proper course was to let him assume his governorship. But Zuo, Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang and acting Governor of Zhejiang, had no intention of giving way. Zeng Guofan requested sick leave for his brother partly out of anxiety over slander and criticism, seeking prudent retirement at the height of success. More fundamentally, he had perceived the hidden uncertainty of his brother’s position. Judging that Guoquan could never take up the post, he thought it better to recognize the situation and withdraw voluntarily.

在朝廷却又能左右为难之苦。一方面东南军务地穴于湖州克复、全浙肃清，不能不敷衍左宗棠的面子；一方面却又觉得真个让簇新的一位伯爵，解甲归田，不是待功臣之道。因此，对于曾国荃告病，一直采拖延着不作明确的处置；希望曾左之间，能够消释嫌怨，言归于好，由左宗棠出面奏请交卸篆，饬令曾国荃到任。这是个不能实现的奢望。朝廷看看拖着不是回事，决定成全曾国藩的心愿，许曾国荃辞职。可是空出来的浙江巡抚这个缺，由谁替补？却颇费斟酌。朝廷也知道左宗棠的意思，最好是让蒋益澧由藩司升任，而浙江藩司一缺，则由左宗棠保荐。无奈蒋益澧的资望还浅；并且这样处置，在曾国藩的面子上太难看。朝廷调和将帅，决不肯轻易予人以偏袒某人的印象，所以左宗棠的意愿是不考虑的了。

The court was in a dilemma. On one hand, military operations in the southeast had culminated in the recovery of Huzhou and the pacification of Zhejiang, so Zuo’s dignity had to be considered. On the other, to let a newly created earl lay down his arms and retire to the countryside seemed an improper way to treat a meritorious servant. The request for Zeng Guoquan’s retirement on grounds of illness was therefore left unresolved. The court hoped that Zeng and Zuo might put aside their resentment and be reconciled, with Zuo himself requesting permission to relinquish the acting governorship and an order for Guoquan to take office. That hope was impossible to fulfill. At last the court saw that indefinite delay would not do and agreed to Guofan’s wish, allowing Guoquan to resign. Who should fill the vacancy, however, required careful thought. The court knew what Zuo wanted: Jiang Yili promoted from provincial treasurer to governor, with the treasury vacancy filled on Zuo’s recommendation. But Jiang lacked sufficient seniority and standing; such an arrangement would also humiliate Zeng Guofan. In balancing its commanders, the court would not lightly give the impression of favoring one man. Zuo’s wishes were therefore ruled out.

要考虑的是∶第一、新任浙江巡抚确需清廉练达的干才，因为洪杨所蹂躏的各省，浙江被祸最惨；善后事宜亦最难办，非清廉干练，不足以胜任。第二、此人要与左宗棠没有什么恩怨；而又能为曾国藩，甚至李鸿章 所支持，然后浙江的善后事宜，才能取得邻省的援助。第三、大乱已平，偃武修文；浙江巡抚是洪杨平后委派的第一员封疆大吏，也是恢复文治的开始，所以此人最好科甲出身。如果有过战功，更为理想。结果选中了一个很理想的人。此人名叫马新贻，字谷山；先世是回回，从明太祖打天下有功，派在山东卫所当武官，定居曹州府荷泽县，已历四百余年之久，因此，马新贻除了信回教以外，彻头彻尾是个山东土著。

Three considerations remained. First, the new Governor of Zhejiang must be honest, experienced, and capable. Of all the provinces ravaged by Hong Xiuquan and Yang Xiuqing, Zhejiang had suffered most, and its reconstruction would be the hardest. Nothing less than integrity and practical ability would suffice. Second, he should have neither obligations nor grievances toward Zuo, while enjoying the support of Zeng Guofan and even Li Hongzhang, so that Zhejiang could obtain its neighbors’ help. Third, with the great rebellion suppressed, arms were to give way to civil government. This would be the first provincial governorship filled since the defeat of the Taipings, marking the restoration of civil rule. The appointee should preferably have risen through the examinations. Military achievements as well would make him ideal. An exceptionally suitable man was eventually chosen: Ma Xinyi, courtesy name Gushan. His ancestors were Hui Muslims who had helped the founding Ming emperor win the empire. Appointed military officers in a Shandong garrison, they settled in Heze County, Caozhou Prefecture. More than four hundred years had passed. Apart from his adherence to Islam, Ma was thoroughly a native son of Shandong.

在马新贻的新命传至浙江的同时；江西来了一个重要而有趣的消息，『幼逆』洪福真终于落网了。收束平洪杨的军务，却还有相当艰巨的戡乱大任，需要部署。恭王、文祥的计议，犹有三处叛乱要平服，才能臻于太平盛世。这三处叛乱是∶第一、南窜的洪杨余孽；第二是扰乱中原的捻匪；第三是荼毒生灵、为患西陲的回乱。幸好人才旺盛，冠绝前朝；恭王与文祥决定托付四个人去平这三处的叛乱。第一个仍然是曾国藩。在十月初一曾国荃功成身退，率领裁撤的湘军回湖南的同时，朝中有一道廷寄递到江宁，说『江宁已臻底平，军务业经藏事，即着曾国藩酌带所部，前赴皖鄂交界，督兵剿贼，务期迅速前进，勿少延缓。』这所谓『贼』，便是捻匪。

As news of Ma Xinyi’s appointment reached Zhejiang, an important and intriguing report arrived from Jiangxi: the young rebel Hong Tianguifu had at last been captured. The campaign against the Taipings was drawing to a close, but formidable work remained before disorder could be put down. In the judgment of Prince Gong and Wenxiang, three rebellions still stood between the empire and lasting peace: the Taiping remnants who had fled south, the Nian bands disturbing the central provinces, and the Muslim rebellions devastating the western frontier. Fortunately, men of talent abounded in numbers surpassing earlier reigns. Prince Gong and Wenxiang decided to entrust the suppression of these three troubles to four men. The first was still Zeng Guofan. On the first day of the tenth month, as Zeng Guoquan retired in triumph and led the disbanded Hunan troops home, a confidential dispatch reached Jiangning: “Jiangning is now entirely pacified, and military operations there are concluded. Zeng Guofan shall select a portion of his forces and proceed to the Anhui–Hubei border to direct the suppression of the rebels. He must advance speedily and permit no delay.” These “rebels” were the Nian.

捻匪原以皖北为老巢，自经僧王全力攻剿，流窜到湖北、河南一带。张洛行虽死，他的侄子张总愚亦非弱者；加以陈玉成的旧部赖文光由关中回窜，因为『天京』已破，成了丧家之犬，自然而然地与捻匪合流，大为猖獗。朝廷深知僧王的马队，追奔逐北，将捻匪撵来撵去的打法，并非善策；一旦疲于奔命，为捻匪反扑，非大败不可。同时，又因为僧王的身分尊贵，连西宫太后都不能不格外优容，是位极难伺候的王爷，指授方略，则『将在外君命有所不受』；稍加督责又怕惹恼了他，索性独断独行。因此，倒不如设法让他交卸军权，回京享福，才是公私两便之计。能代僧王指挥数省的，只有一个曾国藩。不仅威望足够；而且他那『先求稳当，次求变化』，以静制静，稳扎稳打的作风，亦正可救僧王之失。至于筹饷之责，朝廷也想到了一个必不可少的人。

The Nian had originally made northern Anhui their base. Under Prince Sengge Rinchen’s vigorous attacks, they had moved into Hubei and Henan. Though Zhang Luoxing was dead, his nephew Zhang Zongyu was no weak successor. Lai Wenguang, formerly one of Chen Yucheng’s commanders, had also returned from Guanzhong. With the Heavenly Capital fallen, he was a man without a home; naturally he joined the Nian, greatly increasing their strength and boldness. The court knew that the prince’s cavalry tactics—pursuing and driving the Nian from place to place—were unsound. Once his troops exhausted themselves, a rebel counterattack must bring disaster. Yet his exalted position made him extremely difficult to handle. Even the Western Empress Dowager had to show him special indulgence. Offer strategic instructions, and he could invoke the maxim that a commander in the field need not obey every order of his sovereign. Press him a little, and he might take offense and act entirely on his own. It would be better, for public and private reasons alike, to find a way for him to relinquish his command and return to enjoy life in Beijing. Only Zeng Guofan could replace him in directing operations across several provinces. His prestige was sufficient, and his practice of “seeking security first and flexibility afterward”—meeting movement with stillness, advancing steadily from firm positions—would correct the prince’s mistakes. For the financing of the campaign, the court had thought of another indispensable man.

这个人就是李鸿章.上谕派他接替曾国藩，暂署两江总督；江苏巡抚则调慈禧太后的恩人，漕运总督吴棠署理。上谕中虽未明言，曾国藩带兵驻扎皖鄂交界，从路粮台由李鸿章 负其全责；可是这样部署的用意是很明白的，第一，曾、李师生，『有事弟子服其劳』，天经地义；第二，李鸿章 带兵，曾国藩替他筹过饷，如今曾国藩带兵，自然该李鸿章 筹饷；第三，两江最富，是海内最主要的一处饷源，所以谁当两江总督，都有筹饷的责任。这样的安排，就大局而言，不能算错；只是委屈了曾国藩，便宜了李鸿章与吴棠，可也就顾不得那么许多了。

That man was Li Hongzhang. An edict appointed him to act in Zeng’s place as Governor-General of Liangjiang, while Wu Tang, Director-General of Grain Transport and a benefactor of Empress Dowager Cixi, was transferred to act as Governor of Jiangsu. The decree did not expressly state that Li would bear full responsibility for the rear supply bureau supporting Zeng on the Anhui–Hubei frontier, but the intention was plain. First, Zeng and Li were teacher and pupil; it was only proper that “when there is work to be done, the disciple undertakes the labor.” Second, Zeng had raised funds when Li commanded in the field; now their roles should be reversed. Third, Liangjiang was the richest region and a principal source of military revenue, so whoever governed it was bound to provide funds. Viewed in terms of the general situation, the arrangement was sound. It merely disadvantaged Zeng and benefited Li and Wu—but not every consideration could be accommodated.

再有一个是杨岳斌。他是与彭玉麟齐名的水师名将，本名杨载福；因为同治皇帝这一辈，玉牒谱系上第一字为『载』，不免有犯讳的不便，所以改名岳斌。当江宁未克复以前，他已升任陕甘总督；打算赋以敉平回乱的重任。回乱不仅生于陕甘；也生于云南与新疆。云南将次平服，而新疆方兴未艾；朝廷寄望于新封子爵的鲍超，特降温旨，认为新疆平乱，『非得勇略出群如鲍超者，前往剿办，恐难壁垒一新』，所以命曾国藩传旨鲍超，在他回籍葬亲的两月假期一满，『即行由川起程，出关剿办回乱。』恭王和文祥知道鲍超好名，特地拿乾嘉名将杨遇春，与他相提并论，很灌了一番米汤。上谕中说∶『从前回疆用兵，杨遇春即系川省土著，立功边域，彪炳旅常。鲍超务当督率诸国，肃清西陲，威扬万里，以与前贤后先辉映。该提督忠勇性成，接奉此旨，必即遵行，以逼朝廷委任。』话说得很诚挚，而命曾国藩传旨，亦有暗示他帮着催劝之意。无奈曾国藩对湘军的急流勇退，明哲保身，早有定算；鲍超是他的爱将，当然要加意保全，所以只是照例传旨，并不劝驾。

Another man selected was Yang Yuebin, a naval commander whose fame equaled Peng Yulin’s. His original name was Yang Zaifu. Since the first character of the Tongzhi Emperor’s generation in the imperial genealogy was Zai, however, the name risked offending the naming taboo, and he changed it to Yuebin. Before Jiangning fell he had already been appointed Governor-General of Shaanxi and Gansu, with the intention of entrusting him with the suppression of the Muslim rebellion. Such rebellions had broken out not only there but in Yunnan and Xinjiang as well. Yunnan was approaching pacification, while Xinjiang’s troubles were gathering force. For the latter, the court placed its hopes in the newly created viscount Bao Chao. A warmly worded decree declared that without “a man of exceptional courage and strategy such as Bao Chao” it would be difficult to transform the military situation in Xinjiang. Zeng was therefore ordered to transmit instructions that, upon the expiry of Bao’s two-month leave to bury his parent, he should “depart immediately from Sichuan, pass beyond the frontier, and suppress the Muslim rebellion.” Knowing Bao’s love of renown, Prince Gong and Wenxiang flattered him by comparing him with Yang Yuchun, the celebrated general of the Qianlong and Jiaqing reigns. “In former campaigns in the Muslim territories, Yang Yuchun, himself a native of Sichuan, won frontier victories whose glory shone upon the military banners. Bao Chao must lead his forces to pacify the western marches, carrying his fame ten thousand li and matching the splendor of his predecessor. Loyal and brave by nature, he will surely obey upon receiving this decree and fulfill the court’s trust.” The language was most earnest. By requiring Zeng to transmit it, the court also hinted that he should help urge Bao forward. Zeng, however, had long resolved that the Hunan Army should withdraw prudently at the height of its success. Bao was a favorite commander whom he particularly wished to protect. He simply conveyed the edict in the usual way and offered no encouragement to depart.

再有一个朝廷寄以重望的，便是左宗棠。他是现任的闽浙总督，由江西瑞金为鲍超所败，而窜入福建境内的李世贤、汪海洋两大股，顺理成章 地该由他负责清剿。左宗棠不是怕事的人，对此亦自觉当仁不让，义不容辞；可是朝廷一连串的处置，却使他即气又急，愤愤不平。首先大失所望的是，浙江巡抚派了马新贻；蒋益澧落了空，也就等于是他失去了浙江这个地盘。其次是李鸿章 调署两江，名位已在己之上，使他很不舒服。其次是在江西的陕甘总督杨岳斌，奉旨迅即到任；朝廷责成浙江每月拨给陕甘协饷十万两，并先筹措八万银子，作为杨军的开拔费用。为此，左宗棠的肝火很旺，每日接见僚属，大骂曾国藩、李鸿章 和郭嵩焘。这样骂了几天，怒火稍减；想想既不肯辞官归田，就得有声有色地大干一番。军务是有把握的，就是饷源越来越绌，得要找个足智多谋的人，趁马新贻末曾到任以前，好好筹划妥当。

The other man in whom the court placed great hopes was Zuo. As Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang, he was naturally responsible for suppressing the two large forces of Li Shixian and Wang Haiyang, defeated by Bao at Ruijin in Jiangxi and driven into Fujian. Zuo was not a man to shrink from trouble. He regarded the duty as his by right and could not honorably refuse. Yet a succession of court decisions made him angry, anxious, and deeply resentful. His first disappointment was Ma Xinyi’s appointment to Zhejiang. Jiang Yili had been passed over, which meant that Zuo had lost control of the province. Next came Li’s transfer to act as Governor-General of Liangjiang, placing him above Zuo in standing and precedence—a most unpleasant thought. Then Yang Yuebin, still in Jiangxi, was ordered to proceed promptly to his post in Shaanxi and Gansu. Zhejiang was required to contribute a hundred thousand taels a month toward his military expenses and first to raise eighty thousand for his army’s departure. Zuo’s temper flared. Every day, when receiving his staff, he roundly abused Zeng Guofan, Li Hongzhang, and Guo Songtao. After several days his anger abated a little. Since he would not resign and return to farming, he must undertake something substantial and impressive. He was confident of his military ability; the difficulty was an ever-shrinking revenue base. Before Ma arrived, he needed a resourceful man to help arrange matters properly.

这个人自然非胡雪岩莫属。『雪翁，』他说，『你看，挤得我无路可走了！你算算看，我该到哪里筹饷？哪里都难！』两个人将十五行省一个一个地算。除开穷瘠的省份，有饷可筹的富庶之地，都已为他人早着先鞭；江苏、安徽是两江辖区，曾李师弟的势力，根深蒂固；江西沈葆桢，对待曾军的前例，足以令人望而却步；山东、山西供应京饷，而且两省巡抚阎敬铭、沈桂芬清刚精明，都不是好相与的人；湖北食用川盐，在沙市设局征厘，收入相当可观，可是官文是督抚中唯一的一个旗人，有理无理，皆受朝廷袒护，不容易打得进去；至于天府之国的四川，有骆秉章 在那里，顾念旧日宾主之谊，自然不好意思唱一出『取成都』。『福建穷得很；我能筹饷的地方，只有贵省和广东了。东该给我的饷不给；可恨郭筠仙，心目中只认得曾涤生、李少荃。此恨难消！』左宗棠停了一下又说，『至于马谷山，听说倒还讲理；不过既是曾涤生所保，又是李少荃的同年，不见得肯助我一臂。雪翁，你看我该怎么办？』

That man could only be Hu. “Mr Xueyan,” Zuo said, “they have squeezed me until I have nowhere to turn. Where do you think I can raise funds? It is difficult everywhere.” Together they went through the fifteen provinces one by one. Leaving aside the poor provinces, every wealthy source of revenue had already been claimed. Jiangsu and Anhui lay within Liangjiang, where Zeng and his pupil Li were deeply entrenched. Shen Baozhen’s treatment of the Hunan Army in Jiangxi was warning enough. Shandong and Shanxi supplied the capital, and their governors, Yan Jingming and Shen Guifen, were upright, shrewd, and difficult men to deal with. Hubei consumed Sichuan salt, collecting substantial likin revenue through an office at Shashi. But Guanwen was the only bannerman among the governors and governors-general; right or wrong, he enjoyed the court’s protection, and gaining access there would be hard. As for prosperous Sichuan, Luo Bingzhang governed it. Remembering their old relationship as patron and secretary, Zuo could hardly bring himself to play out a “seizure of Chengdu.” “Fujian is desperately poor. The only places left to me are your province and Guangdong. Guangdong withholds the contributions due to me. That hateful Guo Yunxian recognizes no one but Zeng Disheng and Li Shaoquan! I cannot forget it.” Zuo paused. “As for Ma Gushan, I hear he is reasonable enough. But Zeng recommended him, and he passed the examinations in the same year as Li. He may not be willing to help me. Mr Xueyan, what am I to do?”

胡雪岩默然。因为他觉得自己的处境很难，左宗棠的知遇要报答；而浙江是自己的家乡，为左宗棠设谋画策，可不能挨地方父老的骂。胡雪岩一向言词爽利，而且不管天大的难事，一诺无辞；象这样迟疑不答的情形，可说绝无仅有。左宗棠微感诧异，不免追问缘故。『不瞒大人说，我很为难。大人现在只有浙江一个地盘，粮饷当然出在浙江，筹得少了不够用；筹得多了，苦了地方。说起来是我胡某人出的主意；本乡本土，我不大好做人。』雪岩又说，『如果大人兼署浙江巡抚，我还可以出出主意，截长补短，见机行事，总还兼顾得到。现在换了马中丞，我又是分发江西的试用道，是大人奏调我在浙江当差；大人一离浙江，我当然不能再问浙江的公事，善后局的差使亦要交卸，何况其他？』

Hu remained silent. His position was difficult. He must repay Zuo’s recognition and favor, yet Zhejiang was his home province. He could not devise schemes for Zuo that would earn the curses of its people. Hu usually spoke decisively and accepted even the greatest difficulties without hesitation; such a prolonged silence was almost unprecedented. Mildly surprised, Zuo pressed him for an explanation. “To be frank, my lord, I am in a difficult position. Zhejiang is now the only province you can draw upon, so naturally your supplies and pay must come from it. Raise too little, and it will not suffice; raise too much, and the people suffer. Everyone will say it was my idea. Among my own countrymen, that would be an uncomfortable position. If you continued to act as Governor of Zhejiang, I could still suggest ways to balance one source against another and adapt to circumstances, taking both interests into account. But Governor Ma is coming. I am only a probationary circuit intendant assigned to Jiangxi, whom you had transferred here for service. Once you leave Zhejiang, I shall have no right to concern myself with its affairs. I must even hand over my post at the Reconstruction Bureau, let alone anything else.”

他一路说，左宗棠一路点头，等他说完，做个『稍安毋躁』的手势答道∶『你刚才所说的情形，我完全清楚，我们要好好谈谈。万变不离的宗旨是∶雪翁，你仍旧要帮我的忙。怎么个帮法，我们回头再商量，现在先谈你的难处；诚如所言，我现在只有浙江一个地盘，粮饷只有着落在浙江，而且要定一个确数，按月一定汇到，连日子都错不得一天。雪翁，凡事先讲理，后讲情；情理都站得住，还争不过人家，我当然也有我的手段。』胡雪岩不知他最后这几句话，意何所指？只能就事论事，问一事∶『大人预备定一个啥数目？』『你看呢？』左宗棠放低了声音说∶『我们自己人，我告诉你实话∶我的兵，实数一万八千，不过筹饷要宽，照两万三千人算。』胡雪岩的心算极快。士兵每人每月饷银、军粮、器械、弹药、马草，加上营帐、锅碗等等杂支，平均要五两银子；两万三千人就是十一万五千两。另加统帅个人的用途；文案、委员的薪水伙食；送往迎来的应酬费用，每个月非十五万银子不可。

Zuo nodded throughout. When Hu finished, he gestured for patience. “I understand all the circumstances you have described. We must discuss them carefully. Through every change, one principle remains: you must continue to help me. How you are to help we shall consider presently. First, let us deal with your difficulty. As you say, Zhejiang is my only base, and Zhejiang must provide my army’s funds. Moreover, there must be a fixed sum, remitted each month on a fixed date, not one day late. Mr Xueyan, in everything we first establish what is reasonable, then appeal to personal feeling. If both reason and feeling support us and we still cannot prevail, I naturally have methods of my own.” Hu did not know what the last words implied. Keeping to the immediate issue, he asked, “What sum do you intend to fix, my lord?” “What would you suggest?” Zuo lowered his voice. “Between ourselves, I shall tell you the truth. I actually have eighteen thousand men, but funding must allow a margin. We should calculate for twenty-three thousand.” Hu reckoned rapidly. A soldier’s monthly pay, grain, weapons, ammunition, horse fodder, and miscellaneous needs—tents, cooking pots, bowls, and the rest—averaged five taels. Twenty-three thousand men meant a hundred and fifteen thousand taels. Add the commander’s own expenses, the salaries and board of secretaries and commissioned officials, and the costs of hospitality, and no less than a hundred and fifty thousand taels a month would do.

这笔巨数，由浙江独力负担，未免太重；胡雪岩便很婉转地说道∶『闽浙一家。福建拨给浙江的协饷，前后总计，不下三百万两之多；如今福建有事，当然要帮忙。而况大人带的又是浙江的兵，理当浙江支饷。不过，浙江的情形，大人是再明白不过的；如果能够量出为入，事情就好办了。』成语是量入为出，胡雪岩却反过来说，倒也新鲜；左宗棠便捻着八字胡子，含笑问道∶『何以谓之量出为入？倒要请教。』『譬如一碗汤，你也舀，他也舀，到嘴都有限┅┅。』『啊！』左宗棠抢着说道∶『我懂了！我亦本有此意，第一，陕甘的协饷，决不能答应；第二，广东解浙江的协饷，有名无实，我要奏请停拨。』说到这里，他眼珠打转，慢慢地笑了，笑得极其诡秘。

For Zhejiang to bear that enormous sum alone was too much. Hu therefore spoke tactfully. “Fujian and Zhejiang are one family. Over the years, Fujian has contributed at least three million taels toward Zhejiang’s military expenses. Now that Fujian has trouble, we should naturally help. Besides, the troops you command are Zhejiang troops; Zhejiang ought to pay them. But you understand the province’s condition better than anyone. If we could determine our income by our expenditure, matters would be easier.” The usual maxim was to determine expenditure by income; Hu had reversed it, which was something new. Stroking his drooping mustache, Zuo asked with a smile, “What do you mean by determining income by expenditure? I should like to hear.” “Suppose there is a bowl of soup. One man takes a ladleful, another takes a ladleful; very little reaches anyone’s mouth—” “Ah!” Zuo interrupted. “I understand. I had the same thought. First, we absolutely cannot agree to the contribution for Shaanxi and Gansu. Second, Guangdong’s contribution to Zhejiang exists only in name. I shall petition to have it discontinued.” At this his eyes moved from side to side, and a slow, exceedingly secretive smile spread over his face.

这一笑，大有文章.胡雪岩觉得非搞明白不可；便有意套问一句∶『广东的协饷是个画饼，虽不能充饥，看看也是好的。』『不然！奏请停拨，就是要让朝廷知道，这是个画饼。雪翁，』左宗棠突然兴奋了，『你看老夫的手段！画饼要把它变成个又大又厚，足供一饱的大麦饼。你信不信？』『怎么不信？』胡雪岩紧接着问，『大人变这套戏法，可要我做下手？』『当然！少了你，我这套平地抠饼，外带大锯活人的戏法就变不成了。』『大锯活人』四字，虽是戏言，却也刺耳，胡雪岩便用半开玩笑的语气问道∶『大人，你要锯哪一个？』『哪一个？』左宗棠有种狞笑的神色，『锯我那位亲家。』胡雪岩骇然。他早知左宗棠跟郭嵩焘有心病，而此心病，不但未能由时光来冲淡，反有与日俱深之势；但何致于说出『大锯活人』的这样的话来？因此一时楞在那里作声不得。左宗棠的脸上，也收起嬉笑之态，变得相当认真，眼睁得好在，嘴闭得好紧；但眼神闪烁，嘴唇翕动，竟似心湖中起了极大的波澜似的。这就使得胡雪岩越发贯注全神，要听他如何『大锯活人』了。

There was much behind that smile. Hu felt he must understand it and deliberately probed. “Guangdong’s contribution is a picture of a cake. Though it cannot feed us, it is something to look at.” “No. By asking for its cancellation, I shall show the court that it is only a painted cake. Mr Xueyan—” Zuo suddenly grew excited. “Watch this old man’s methods! I shall turn the painted cake into a great thick barley cake, enough to fill our bellies. Do you believe me?” “Of course. Will you need me as an assistant in this conjuring trick?” “Naturally! Without you I could never perform this trick of producing a cake from bare ground—and sawing a living man in two besides.” Though meant as a joke, the last words were jarring. Half in jest, Hu asked, “Whom do you mean to saw in two, my lord?” “Whom?” Zuo’s smile had grown fierce. “My own in-law.” Hu was appalled. He had long known that Zuo bore a grievance against Guo Songtao, one that time had deepened rather than eased. But how had it reached the point of such language? For a moment he stood speechless. Zuo too ceased smiling. His face grew serious, his eyes wide, his mouth firmly closed; yet his gaze flickered and his lips moved, as though powerful waves were passing through his mind. Hu listened with even closer attention to hear how this “sawing a living man in two” was to be done.

『雪岩！』左宗棠第一次改口，以别字相呼，表示对胡雪岩以密友看待，『你的书读得不多，我是知道的；不过「世事洞明皆学问」，照这一层来说，我佩服你。』『不敢当。』胡雪岩有些局促，但也很率直，『大人有什么话要说，尽管吩咐；拿顶「高帽子」套在我头上，就有点吃不消了。』『你我之间，何用要什么送高帽子的手段？我的意思是，我的为人，我的处世，只有你能明白五分；还有五分，你不但不明白，或许还会大不以为然。这就因为你少读书；如果你也多读过一点书，就会明白我那另外五分，而且谅解我不得不然；势所必然！』原来如此，胡雪岩倒有些受宠若惊了，『大人』他说∶『你老跟我谈「大家之道，在明明德」，我是不懂的。』『我不跟你谈经，我跟你谈史。雪岩，我先请问你两句成语，「大义灭亲」、「公而忘私」怎么讲？』

“Xueyan!” For the first time Zuo dropped the formal address and used his courtesy name, treating him as an intimate friend. “I know you have not read many books. But understanding the world is itself learning, and in that respect I admire you.” “You are too kind.” Hu was a little uneasy but remained frank. “If you have something to say, please give me your instructions. Such a tall hat of praise is rather too much for me.” “Why should I need flattery between us? What I mean is that you understand half of my character and conduct. The other half you not only fail to understand, but may strongly disapprove of. That is because you have read too little. If you had studied more, you would understand that other half as well, and see that I have no choice: circumstances compel it.” So that was what he meant. Hu felt almost overwhelmed by the confidence shown him. “My lord, if you speak to me of ‘the Way of Great Learning lies in manifesting luminous virtue,’ I shall understand nothing.” “I shall speak of history, not the Classics. First, tell me what these two sayings mean: ‘For a greater righteousness, sacrifice even one’s kin,’ and ‘For public duty, forget private interests.’”

胡雪岩无以为答；觉得也不必答，老实回复∶『大人不要考我了。就从这两句成语上头，谈你老的打算。』『我不是考你，我的意思是，我的行事，照世俗之见，或许会大大地骂我。不过，我的行事，于亲有亏，于义无悖；于私有惭，于公无愧。这都非世俗之见所能谅解，而只有读过书的人，才会在心里说一声∶左某人命世之英，不得不然。』这段话很掉了几句文，不过胡雪岩也大致还能听得懂；而且听出意思，他对郭嵩焘要下辣手了！所想不通的是，他有何辣手可对郭嵩焘？他的疑问，立刻得到了解答；左宗棠起身坐在书桌前面，伸毫铺纸，很快地画成一幅地图，在那些曲线、圆点之中，写上地名；胡雪岩看出是一幅闽粤交界的形势图。『李世贤在漳州。漳州是九月十四沦陷的，总兵禄魁阵亡；汀漳龙道徐晓峰殉难。李世贤大概有八千多人，不可轻敌。』左宗棠又指着长汀、连城、上杭这三角地带说∶『汪海洋在这一带；照我的看法，他比李世贤更凶悍。然而，不足为虑，贼不足平！雪岩，你这几年总也懂得一点兵法了！你看李、汪二贼的出路在哪里？』

Hu had no answer, nor felt one was needed. He replied honestly, “Please do not examine me, my lord. Begin with those sayings and tell me your plans.” “I am not examining you. My point is that ordinary people may condemn my actions bitterly. Yet though I fail my kin, I do not fail what is right; though I may be ashamed in private relationships, I have nothing to blush for in public duty. Common opinion cannot understand this. Only a learned man will say in his heart: ‘Zuo is a hero born for his age. He could do no otherwise.’” The speech was rather bookish, but Hu understood it well enough and grasped its implication: Zuo meant to deal Guo Songtao a severe blow. What he could not see was what blow lay within Zuo’s power. His question was answered at once. Zuo rose, sat at his desk, took a brush, and spread out paper. He rapidly drew a map, adding place-names among the curved lines and dots. Hu recognized the Fujian–Guangdong frontier. “Li Shixian is at Zhangzhou, which fell on the fourteenth day of the ninth month. Brigade Commander Lukui was killed in action; Circuit Intendant Xu Xiaofeng of Tingzhou, Zhangzhou, and Longyan died at his post. Li has probably more than eight thousand men and must not be underestimated.” Pointing to the triangle formed by Changting, Liancheng, and Shanghang, Zuo continued, “Wang Haiyang is here. In my judgment he is fiercer than Li. Still, there is no cause for alarm about putting these rebels down. Xueyan, you must have learned a little strategy in recent years. Where do you think Li and Wang can escape?”

这一下好象考倒了胡雪岩。他仔细看了半天，方始答说『他们是由西面江西逃过来的；往东是出海，有好长一段路，再说没有船也出不了海。北面呢，大人带兵压了下来，啊，』胡雪岩恍然大悟，很有把握地说∶『这两个长毛的出路，只有南面的广东，嘉应州首当其冲！』左宗棠深深点头，拈髭微笑，『对，』他说，『嘉应州首当其冲！到了那时候充饥的就不是画饼了！』语中有深意。左宗棠没有说下去；胡雪岩不便回——怕自己猜错了，冒昧一关，是大大的失言。谁知左宗棠毫不忌讳，真的拿胡雪岩当可共极端机密的心腹看待，『郭筠仙一直担心曾涤生「驱寇入粤」，他没有想到「驱寇入粤」的是他的亲家。』他说∶『雪岩，到那时候，又另是一番局面了。』胡雪岩不自觉地打了个寒噤，觉得左宗棠的手段真是太辣了些！虽然，这正是他所猜想到的，但测度是测度，听别人亲口证实，感觉又自不同。

For a moment Hu seemed stumped. He studied the map closely before answering. “They came from Jiangxi in the west. To the east lies the sea, a long way off—and without ships they could not put to sea anyway. In the north, your troops are pressing down. Ah!” Understanding came suddenly, and he spoke with confidence. “Their only way out is south into Guangdong. Jiaying Prefecture will bear the first attack.” Zuo nodded deeply, stroking his mustache with a smile. “Exactly. Jiaying will bear the first attack. Then we shall no longer be feeding ourselves on painted cakes.” There was a hidden meaning in his words. He did not continue, and Hu dared not ask, fearing that a mistaken guess might lead him into a grave indiscretion. Zuo, however, had no such reservations. He truly regarded Hu as a confidant fit to hear the deepest secrets. “Guo Yunxian has always feared that Zeng Disheng would drive the rebels into Guangdong. He never imagined it would be his own in-law who did so. When that happens, Xueyan, the situation will be entirely different.” Hu shuddered involuntarily. Zuo’s methods seemed altogether too ruthless. He had guessed this very thing, certainly; but a conjecture was one matter, and hearing it confirmed in the man’s own words was another.

『雪岩，』左宗棠问道∶『你倒说说看到那时候是怎么样的一番局面？』『是。』胡雪岩想了想说，『到那时候，朝廷当然借重大人的威望，拜钦差大臣，节制福建、浙江、广东三省的军务。郭中丞——。』他没有再说下去；意思是郭嵩焘在左宗棠『大锯活人』的摆布之下，非吃足苦头不可。『不错，此亦是势所必然之事。到那时候，雪岩，我不会再累浙江了，不怕郭筠仙不乖乖替我筹饷。不过，』左宗棠沉吟了好一会，『也说不定！郭筠仙愚而好自用；怕他仍旧执迷不悟。』『果然如此，大人又怎么办？』

“Xueyan, tell me what the situation will be then.” “Yes.” Hu considered. “The court will naturally turn to your prestige and ability, appoint you imperial commissioner, and place military affairs in Fujian, Zhejiang, and Guangdong under your authority. Governor Guo—” He stopped. His meaning was clear: under Zuo’s handling, Guo would suffer severely. “Precisely. Circumstances must lead to that. Then, Xueyan, I shall no longer burden Zhejiang. Guo Yunxian will have to raise funds obediently for me. Unless—” Zuo pondered for a long while. “There is no certainty. Guo is foolish and obstinate. He may still refuse to see reason.” “And if he does, my lord, what will you do?”

『那就不能怪我了！可惜！』前后两句话不接气，胡雪岩再机敏也猜不透他的意思；只以此事于减轻浙江的负担关系甚大，不能不追问∶『大人，可惜些什么？』『可惜，我夹袋里没有可以当巡抚的人物。』这是说，如果将来郭嵩焘不能替左宗棠筹得足够的饷；他不惜攻倒他派人取而代之。这样做法，却真是『公而忘私』、『大义灭亲』了。『到时候看吧！言之过早。』左宗棠对着他手绘的地图凝视了好一会，突然拍案而起，『对，就是这么办！』

“Then he cannot blame me. What a pity!” The two remarks seemed disconnected. Quick-witted as he was, Hu could not guess their meaning. Since the matter concerned a possible reduction of Zhejiang’s burden, he had to ask. “A pity in what respect, my lord?” “A pity I have no suitable man in reserve to become a governor.” In other words, if Guo Songtao failed to raise enough money for him, Zuo would not hesitate to bring him down and put someone else in his place. That would indeed be “forgetting private interests for public duty” and “sacrificing kin for a greater righteousness.” “We shall see when the time comes. It is too early to speak of it.” Zuo stared for some time at his map. Suddenly he struck the desk and sprang up. “Yes! That is how it shall be done!”

接着，左宗棠谈了他的突如其来的灵感。他指着地图为胡雪岩解释，自己的兵力还不够；倘或想用三面包抄的办法，将长毛向广东方面挤，相当吃力。万一有个漏洞填塞不住，长毛一出了海，不管在福建或浙江的海面，自己都脱不了干系，岂不是弄巧成拙？因此，左宗棠想请李鸿章 的淮军助以一臂。克复湖州之役，彼此合作得还满意；如今再申前请，想来李鸿章 不致于拒绝。『不过，这话我不便开口。』左宗棠说，『如果是我出面相邀，就得替客军筹饷；譬如他派一万人，一个月起码就得五六五银子，再加上开拔的盘缠，第一笔就非拨十万银子不可，实在力有未逮。倘或朝廷有旨意，让淮军自备粮饷，来闽助剿；我们至多备五万银子作犒赏，面子上也就把好看了。雪岩，你说，我这把如意算盘如何？』『是好算盘。不过淮军自备粮饷，恐怕李中丞不肯。他出饷，我们出粮；李中丞就没话好说了，因为他的军队闲摆在那里，一样也是要发饷的。至于请朝廷降旨，只有请福建的京官在京里活动。』『那怕不行。』左宗棠摇摇头，『福建京官，目前没有身居高位的，说话不大有力量。闽浙唇齿相依。浙江在京的大老，雪岩你倒想想看，有什么人可托？『

He explained his sudden inspiration, pointing to the map. His forces were still insufficient. Enveloping the rebels on three sides and squeezing them toward Guangdong would be difficult. If one gap remained unblocked and the rebels escaped to sea, whether off Fujian or Zhejiang, he would still bear responsibility. Would that not defeat his own purpose? He therefore wished to enlist Li Hongzhang’s Anhui Army. Their cooperation at Huzhou had been satisfactory; surely Li would not refuse another request. “But I cannot make the approach myself,” Zuo said. “If I invite them, I must fund the visiting troops. Suppose he sends ten thousand men: that means at least fifty or sixty thousand taels a month. Add their departure expenses, and the first allocation must be a hundred thousand. That is beyond me. If the court orders the Anhui Army to bring its own pay and provisions and assist in Fujian, we need provide no more than fifty thousand as a reward. That would satisfy appearances. Xueyan, what do you think of my calculation?” “It is a good one. But Governor Li may refuse to provide both pay and food. If he supplies the pay and we the grain, he will have nothing to object to. His men must be paid even if they remain idle. As for obtaining an imperial order, we must ask Fujian officials in Beijing to work for it.” “That may not succeed.” Zuo shook his head. “No Fujian man there currently holds a sufficiently high position; their words carry little weight. Fujian and Zhejiang depend on one another like lips and teeth. Think of the senior Zhejiang men in Beijing. Whom could we approach?”

『浙江在京的大老，自然要数许大人；不过，他的吏部尚书交卸了。倒是他的大少爷，在南书房很红；还有他一位侄少爷，是小军机，专管军务——。』『对！对！』不等胡雪岩说完，左宗棠便抢着说，『这条路子再好都没有，请你替我进行。许家杭州望族，你总有熟人吧？』『他家的人很多，我倒认得几痊；不过象这样的大事，也不好随便托人。』胡雪岩想了一会说，『大人，我想到上海去一趟；去看许七大人。一面拿大人交办的事托他；一面想拿许七大人搬到杭州，出面来办善后。』左宗棠想了一下。觉得胡雪岩这个办法极好——所谓『许七大人』就是小刀会刘丽川起事之时的江苏巡抚许乃钊；如今逃难在上海。他的胞兄，也就是胡雪岩口中的『许六大人』许乃普，以吏部尚书致仕，因为闹长毛不能南归；在京里是浙江同乡的『家乡』。而且科名前辈，久掌文衡，京中大老，颇加尊礼。许乃普的长子许彭寿，是李鸿章 的同年，也是道光二十七年丁未这一榜的会元；许乃普还有个胞侄许庚皋，在『辛酉政变』中出过大力，如今是极红的『小军机』——军机章京领班之一，熟谙兵事，精于方略，对军务部署有极大的发言权。所以走这条路子，路路皆通；必要时还可以请许彭寿以同年的交情，写封切切实实的信给李鸿章 ，更无有不能如愿之理。

“Among the senior Zhejiang men, Lord Xu naturally comes first. But he has retired from the Ministry of Personnel. His eldest son, however, is much favored in the Southern Study. He also has a nephew in the Grand Council secretariat, dealing particularly with military affairs—” “Exactly! Exactly!” Zuo interrupted. “There could be no better approach. Please arrange it for me. The Xu family is one of Hangzhou’s great clans. Surely you know someone?” “There are many of them, and I know several. But a matter of this importance cannot be entrusted to just anyone.” Hu thought a moment. “I should like to go to Shanghai and see Seventh Master Xu. I can put your business before him and at the same time try to persuade him to return to Hangzhou and take charge of reconstruction.” After considering, Zuo found this an excellent plan. “Seventh Master Xu” was Xu Naizhao, Governor of Jiangsu at the time of Liu Lichuan’s Small Swords uprising, now living as a refugee in Shanghai. His elder brother, Hu’s “Sixth Master Xu,” was Xu Naipu, retired Minister of Personnel. Unable to return south because of the rebels, he had become a kind of home away from home for Zhejiang men in Beijing. A senior examination graduate who had long presided over literary selection, he was treated with particular respect by the capital’s elders. His eldest son, Xu Pengshou, had graduated in the same cohort as Li Hongzhang and headed the metropolitan examination list in the dingwei year, the twenty-seventh of Daoguang. Xu Naipu also had a nephew, Xu Gengshen, who had rendered important service during the Xinyou coup. Now a highly favored senior secretary of the Grand Council, he understood military affairs and strategy and exercised considerable influence over deployments. This route opened doors in every direction. If necessary, Xu Pengshou could use his fellowship with Li to write him a particularly earnest letter. There was every reason to expect success.

至于将许乃钊请回杭州来主持善后，这也是一着非下不可的好棋。因为马新贻一到任，胡雪岩有不得不走之势；而要找替手，最适当的人选就是许乃钊。第一，他做过封疆大吏，科名是翰林出身，名副其实的『缙绅先生』；第二，马新贻不仅是许乃钊的后辈，而且与他的胞侄许彭寿同榜，以『老世叔』的身分去看马新贻，照例应受『硬进硬出』——开中门迎送的礼遇，这样为地方讲话就有力量就得多了；第三，许乃钊公正廉洁，德高望重，足以冠冤群伦。因此，左宗棠欣然接纳胡雪岩的建设；而且自己表示，要亲笔写封很恳切的信，向许乃钊致意。

Bringing Xu Naizhao back to direct Hangzhou’s reconstruction was likewise an excellent and necessary move. Once Ma arrived, Hu would have to leave, and Xu was the best possible replacement. First, he had governed a province and risen through the Hanlin Academy, a gentleman of established rank in every sense. Second, Ma was not only his junior but a fellow graduate of his nephew Xu Pengshou. Visiting Ma in the position of an honored uncle of the older generation, Xu would be entitled to the formal courtesy of the central gate being opened for his arrival and departure. His voice on local affairs would carry correspondingly greater weight. Third, he was just, incorruptible, and universally respected, eminently qualified to lead the local gentlemen. Zuo therefore gladly accepted Hu’s proposal and offered to write Xu a most earnest personal letter.

谈完了公事谈『私事』；而私事也就是公事∶胡雪岩的出处。左宗棠打算将他调到福建；但不必随他一起行动，专驻上海，为他经理一切。胡雪岩毫不迟疑地答应了下来。从第二天起，左宗棠便照商定的步骤，积极开始部署；除了战报以外，一连拜发了好几道奏折。第一道是∶浙江的兵饷军需，十分困难，自顾不暇；应该拨给陕甘的协饷，请饬户部另筹改拨。第二道是，请饬新任浙江巡抚马新贻，从速到任，至于马新贻未到任前，浙江巡抚请由藩司蒋益澧『护理』。第三道是，奉旨拨解杨岳斌的『行资』八万两，于无可设法之中，勉强设法筹拨半数。

With public business settled, they turned to “private” business, which was itself public: Hu’s future position. Zuo intended to have him transferred to Fujian. He need not travel with the army, however; he would remain in Shanghai and manage all Zuo’s affairs there. Hu agreed without hesitation. From the following day, Zuo energetically began carrying out their agreed steps. Besides military reports, he sent several memorials in succession. The first pleaded that Zhejiang could scarcely meet its own army’s needs and asked the Ministry of Revenue to find another source for the contribution to Shaanxi and Gansu. The second urged Ma Xinyi to take office quickly and requested that Provincial Treasurer Jiang Yili temporarily administer the governorship until his arrival. The third stated that, of the eighty thousand taels ordered for Yang Yuebin’s departure expenses, only half had been raised, and that with the greatest difficulty.

第四道奏折与浙江无关——每天夏秋之交，户部照例催各省报解『京饷』；京饷不止于发放在京八旗禁军的粮饷，举凡王公大臣，文武百官的廉俸；大小衙门办公的经费；宗庙陵寝的祭祀费用；以及专供两宫太后及皇帝私人花用，每年分三节呈上的『交进银』，无不出在京饷之内，所以协饷可欠，京饷不可欠。福建欠海关税银十万两；茶税二万两，上谕催解∶『务于十二月内，尽数解齐。倘仍饰辞宕延，致误要需，即由户部查照奏定章 程，指名严参。』虽奉这样的严旨，左宗棠仍要欠上一次；因为非如此，不足以表示福建之穷，必须浙江接济。当然，欠有欠的方法，不是硬顶可以了事的；左宗棠的方法是，哭穷之外，将他闽浙总督应得的『养廉银』一万两，由票号汇到户部，作为京饷报解。

The fourth concerned Fujian. Every year, as summer passed into autumn, the Ministry of Revenue pressed the provinces to remit their contributions to the capital. These paid not merely the Eight Banner guards but the salaries and allowances of princes, ministers, and officials; the expenses of government offices; sacrifices at ancestral temples and imperial tombs; and the silver presented at three annual festivals for the personal use of the emperor and the two empress dowagers. Provincial military contributions might fall into arrears; the capital’s funds could not. Fujian owed a hundred thousand taels in customs revenue and twenty thousand in tea tax. An edict demanded payment in full during the twelfth month and threatened named impeachments under the prescribed rules if further excuses delayed essential expenditure. Despite this stern order, Zuo meant to default once more. Only thus could he demonstrate Fujian’s poverty and its need for Zhejiang’s help. Yet default required method; blunt defiance would not suffice. Besides pleading poverty, he remitted his own ten-thousand-tael governor-general’s integrity allowance through a draft bank to the Ministry of Revenue, to be credited toward the capital’s funds.

第五道是请停止广东解浙的协饷。主要的作用是借此机会让朝廷知道，广东的协饷，对浙江来说是个『画饼』。所以，停止的理由，不过『现在浙省军务肃清，所有前项协饷，自应停止』这样一句；而『停止』以前的帐目，却算得很清楚，从同治元年正月到这年八月，连闰共计三十三个月；广东应解浙江协饷三百三十万两，可是实收仅二十八万。其中由厘金所拨者是二十二万两；曾国藩奏道，广东厘金开办起至这年八月底止，共收一百二十万，是则浙军『所得不过十成之二』。

The fifth memorial requested an end to Guangdong’s military contributions to Zhejiang. Its chief purpose was to show the court that these contributions had been no more than a painted cake. The stated reason for discontinuance was brief: “Military operations in Zhejiang having now ended, the above contributions should naturally cease.” But the preceding accounts were set out precisely. From the first month of the first Tongzhi year to the eighth month of the current year, including the intercalary month, thirty-three months had elapsed. Guangdong should have remitted three million three hundred thousand taels. Zhejiang had actually received only two hundred and eighty thousand, of which two hundred and twenty thousand came from likin. Zeng Guofan had reported that Guangdong’s likin receipts, from the levy’s introduction to the end of that eighth month, totaled one million two hundred thousand taels. Thus Zhejiang’s army had received “not even two-tenths.”

第六道是部署到福建以后的人事。奏折的案由是『办理饷需各员，请旨奖励』；附带请求调用。其中当然有胡雪岩，他本来是『盐运使衔』的『江西试用道』；左宗棠奏请『改发福建以道员补用，并请赏加按察使衔』，这报奖的文字，看来并不如武官的『请赏戴花翎』、『请赏加巴图鲁称号』来得热闹起眼；其实帮了胡雪岩很大的一个忙，因为由『试用道』改为『以道员补用』，只要一准，立刻可以补任何实缺；而『赏加按察使衔』，便可以署理阜司，成为实缺道员更上层楼的『监司大员』。在左宗棠来说，这一保，起码等于三年的劳绩。

The sixth memorial concerned personnel after the move to Fujian. Its heading requested rewards for officials who had managed military supplies and funding; it also sought their transfer. Hu was naturally included. He was then a probationary circuit intendant assigned to Jiangxi, holding the honorary rank of salt commissioner. Zuo asked that he be “reassigned to Fujian for substantive appointment as a circuit intendant, and granted the honorary rank of provincial judicial commissioner.” Such wording looked less splendid than military requests for a peacock feather or the title of baturu. In reality, it did Hu a tremendous service. Once approved, the change from probationary status to eligibility for substantive appointment meant that he could immediately fill any vacant circuit intendancy. The judicial commissioner’s honorary rank would also qualify him to act in that higher office, rising above an ordinary circuit post into the senior provincial administration. Zuo’s recommendation was worth at least three years of service.

不过左宗棠拜发这道奏折时，胡雪岩并不知道；因为他人已到了上海。拿着左宗棠的亲笔函件去见『许七大人』；谈得十分融洽。将左宗棠所托之事，一一办妥；只不过耽搁了两夜，陪老母谈一谈劫后的西湖，与古应春盘桓了半天，便即原船回到杭州。回到杭州，第一个要想见他的不是左宗棠，而是藩司『护理抚篆』的蒋益澧；他早就派人在阜康钱庄留下话，等胡雪岩一到，立刻通知，以便会面。『雪翁，』与胡雪岩见着了面，蒋益澧哭丧着脸说∶『你非帮我的忙不可！大帅交代下来了，浙江每个月解福建协饷二十万两；按月十二号汇出，迟一天都不准。这不是强人所难吗？』听得这话，胡雪岩也吓一跳。洪杨之乱，浙江遭劫特深，满目疮痛，百废待举，何来每月二十万两银子，供养入闽之师？当时估计，每月能凑十万两银子，已经至矣尽矣；不想左宗棠狮子大开口，加了一倍，而且日子都不准托，这就未免太过分了。

Hu knew nothing of this memorial when Zuo sent it, for he had already reached Shanghai. Carrying Zuo’s personal letter, he called on Seventh Master Xu, and their conversation went most agreeably. He completed all the business entrusted to him, stayed only two nights, spoke with his aged mother of West Lake after the devastation, spent half a day with Gu Yingchun, and returned to Hangzhou in the same boat. The first man seeking him there was not Zuo but Jiang Yili, the provincial treasurer temporarily administering the governorship. Jiang had already left word at Fukang Bank that he was to be notified the moment Hu arrived, so that they could meet. “Mr Xueyan,” he said with a miserable expression, “you must help me. The commander has ordered Zhejiang to send Fujian two hundred thousand taels every month, remitted on the twelfth without a single day’s delay. Is that not asking the impossible?” Hu too was startled. Zhejiang had suffered especially grievously in the Taiping war; devastation lay everywhere, and everything awaited rebuilding. Where could it find two hundred thousand taels a month to support an army entering Fujian? Hu had reckoned that scraping together a hundred thousand would already strain the province to the utmost. Now Zuo demanded twice that amount and would not even permit a delay in payment. It was excessive.

『雪翁，』蒋益澧又说，『于公于私，你都不能不说话，私，老兄在大帅面前言听计从；公，俗语说的「羊毛出在羊身上」，真是逼得非解这个数目不可，只有让地方受累。雪翁，你也于心不忍吧！再说，我到底不过是藩司。』最后这句话，才是蒋益澧真正的苦衷。目前巡抚的大印握在手里，令出即行，办事还容易；等马新贻一到任，认为协饷数目太大要减，他当藩司的，不能不听命。而另一方面左宗棠又是一手提拔他的恩主，且有承诺在先，不能不维持原数。这一下岂非挤在夹缝里轧扁了头？想了一会，胡雪岩觉得这个麻烦非揽下来不可，便点点头说∶『好的。我来想办法。』『这一来有救了！』蒋益澧如释重负，拱拱手问说∶『雪翁，谅来胸来成竹了。是何办法，可以不可以先闻为快？』『当然，当然！原要请教。』胡雪岩答说，『第一，我想请左大人酌减数目。』『酌减？』蒋益澧问，『减多少？』『总得打个七折。』

“On both public and private grounds, you must speak,” Jiang continued. “Privately, the commander listens to you and follows your advice. Publicly, as the saying goes, wool must come from the sheep. If this sum is forced from us, the people must suffer. You could not bear that either. Besides, I am, after all, only the provincial treasurer.” That last sentence revealed his real distress. For the moment he held the governor’s seal and could issue effective orders. Once Ma arrived, however, if the new governor considered the contribution excessive and ordered a reduction, Jiang would have to obey. Yet Zuo was the patron who had raised him, and Jiang had already undertaken to maintain the original sum. Would he not be crushed between the two? After thinking it over, Hu concluded that he must take this difficulty upon himself. He nodded. “Very well. I shall find a way.” “Then there is hope!” Relieved, Jiang clasped his hands and asked, “I imagine you already have a plan. Might I hear it?” “Of course. I wished to consult you. First, I shall ask Lord Zuo to reduce the amount.” “Reduce it by how much?” “At least by thirty percent.”

『打个七折，每月亦还得要十四万两。』蒋益澧说∶『如今军务肃清，我这个藩司不必带兵打仗，要在本分上做点事。你看——。』蒋益澧细数他该做的事，最有关国计民生的要政，便是兴修水利。浙江全境皆是土田，近山者瘠，近水者腴。兼以蚕丝之利，首重栽桑；而桑树的栽培灌溉，与水田的要求，没有什么两样。所以自古以来，在浙江做官，而遗爱在民，久留去思的，无不是因为在水利方面大有成就之故。

“That would still be a hundred and forty thousand a month,” Jiang said. “Now that the province is pacified, I need no longer command troops. I ought to accomplish something in my proper office. Consider—” He listed his duties. The most important for the economy and the people’s livelihood was the repair of waterworks. Zhejiang was a land of cultivated fields: those near the hills were poor, those near water rich. Silk production made mulberry cultivation particularly important, and mulberries required much the same irrigation as paddy fields. Since ancient times, officials whose kindness was long remembered in Zhejiang had invariably distinguished themselves in water management.

浙江的水利重在浙北；浙北的水利父重在海塘。乾隆六次南巡，都以巡视浙江海塘为名，可以想见其关系的重大。海塘欲求完固足以捍御海潮，须用石塘；洪杨作乱以来，海宁一带的石塘没有修过，日渐坍圮，现在要及时修复，估计费用须上百万银子；迫不得已，只有先办土塘，暂且将就。『就是办土塘，亦要三十万银子。土塘料不贵，人工贵；大乱之后，壮丁少了，就是人工费。』蒋益澧说，『雪翁，这件事我亦要跟你好好商量；怎么筹得一笔款子，拿海塘修一修？万一海塘溃决，可是件不得了的事，一想起来，我真连觉都睡不着。』听蒋益澧这样表示，即令是娇饰之词，胡雪岩亦是十分可敬。『三代以下惟恐不好名』，他的本心不必问。听他的语气是想做好官；正不妨与人为善，趁此机会捧他一捧、扶他一扶，拿他逼到好官的路上，亦正是地方之福。想到这里，他毫不迟疑地答道∶『请放心。我来策划一下，大家量力捐办，不是难事。』『那就再好没有。』蒋益澧很欣慰地，『还有西湖的疏浚，也不能再拖了。西湖水利，关乎杭州、海宁的水田灌溉；明年春天以前，一定要整理好，这也得好几万银子。雪翁，你倒想，我这个藩司难做不难做？有啥开源之道，真要好好向你请教。』『如今只有在盐上动脑筋。』胡雪岩答说，『倘能照我的办法，可以救得一时之急，一年半载，福建军务，告个段落；浙江不必再负担协饷，那时候就轻松了。』『我也是这么想，不过，盐法我不大懂；大帅倒是内行。』『左大人是内行？』胡雪岩很惊异地问。

The chief concern was northern Zhejiang, and there the sea dikes were paramount. The Qianlong Emperor had made inspection of these dikes the stated purpose of all six southern tours—proof enough of their importance. To withstand the tides, they needed to be built of stone. Since the rebellion, the stone dikes around Haining had received no repairs and were steadily crumbling. Restoration would cost more than a million taels. With no alternative, temporary earthen works would have to suffice. “Even earth dikes will cost three hundred thousand,” Jiang said. “The materials are cheap; labor is dear. After the great disorder, there are fewer able-bodied men, which makes labor expensive. We must discuss how to raise money for repairs. If the sea dikes give way, the consequences will be terrible. The thought keeps me awake.” Even if this display was affected, Hu found it worthy of respect. “Since the Three Dynasties, the danger is only that men may not care for a good name.” Jiang’s deepest motives need not be examined. He sounded as though he wanted to be a good official. Hu might as well encourage and support him, pressing him into that path for the province’s benefit. “Do not worry,” he answered at once. “I shall make a plan. Let everyone contribute according to his means; it should not be difficult.” “That would be excellent.” Jiang was pleased. “The dredging of West Lake cannot wait either. Its waters irrigate fields in Hangzhou and Haining. Everything must be put in order before next spring, and that too will cost tens of thousands of taels. Is a treasurer’s task easy? I must ask your advice on new revenue.” “For the present, salt is our only resource. My method could tide us over. In six months or a year, the Fujian campaign should reach a conclusion, and Zhejiang will no longer have to contribute. Then things will be easier.” “I think so too. But I know little of salt administration. The commander is an expert.” “Lord Zuo is an expert?” Hu asked in surprise.

『这也无足为怪的。雪翁，你莫非不知道？大帅是陶文毅公的儿女亲家。』『啊！啊！原来如此！』胡雪岩恍然大悟，左宗棠对盐法内行，渊源有自。在他廿六岁时，两江总督陶澍在江西阅兵事毕，请假顺道回湖南安化原籍扫墓，经过醴陵，县官照例『办差』，布置公馆时，请主讲醴陵渌江书院的左宗棠，做了一副对联，陶澍一见，激赏不已；问知县官，出自左宗棠的手笔，当时便请来相见。果然，一谈到浙江的盐务，左宗棠立即表示，在他交卸浙江巡抚兼职以前，有几件必办的事，其中之一是就是整顿浙江盐务，改引行票，打算从同冶四年正月起，先试办一年。

“Nothing surprising about that. Do you not know? The commander’s family is joined by marriage to that of Lord Tao, posthumously honored as Wenyi.” “Ah! So that is it!” Hu suddenly understood. Zuo’s knowledge of salt administration had a history. When Zuo was twenty-six, Tao Shu, Governor-General of Liangjiang, had completed an inspection of troops in Jiangxi and obtained leave to visit the ancestral graves at his native Anhua in Hunan. Passing through Liling, he was received with the customary official arrangements. While preparing his residence, the magistrate asked Zuo, then head of the Lujiang Academy at Liling, to compose a couplet. Tao admired it immensely. Learning who had written it, he immediately sent for Zuo. Sure enough, when Hu raised Zhejiang’s salt administration, Zuo declared at once that reforming it was one of the tasks he must complete before relinquishing the acting governorship. He intended to replace the quota-certificate system with salt permits, beginning in the first month of the fourth Tongzhi year, on a one-year trial.

『我的办法，一共四款∶第一是缉私；第二是革浮费；第三是减价；第四是清查煎盐的灶户。至于盐课收入，全数提为军饷；除去开销每个月至少有十万银子，够我一半的数目了。』这就是说，左宗棠援闽之师，每个月要浙江负担二十万两的饷银。与蒋益澧的话，完全相符。胡雪岩很沉着，暂且放在心；先谈盐务。『大人这四款办法，后面三条是办得到的；就是缉私有些难处。浙盐行销松江；松江是江苏地面，鞭长莫及。这一层可曾想过？』『当然想过。』左宗棠答道，『我正要跟你商量，你不是跟我提过，有个松江漕帮的首脑，人很诚朴能干吗？他肯不肯帮帮浙江的忙？』『此人姓尤，只要大人吩咐，他一定乐予效劳。』胡雪岩问道∶『就不知道这个忙怎么帮法？』

“My plan has four parts,” Zuo said. “First, suppress smuggling; second, abolish irregular fees; third, reduce prices; fourth, conduct a proper registration of salt-producing households. All salt-tax receipts will go to the army. After expenses, there should be at least a hundred thousand taels a month—enough for half my requirement.” So Zhejiang was indeed expected to provide two hundred thousand a month for his Fujian campaign, exactly as Jiang had said. Hu remained composed and set that aside for the moment, speaking first of salt. “The last three parts can be carried out. Suppressing smuggling will be more difficult. Zhejiang salt is sold in Songjiang, which is Jiangsu territory and beyond our reach. Have you considered that?” “Certainly. I was going to discuss it with you. Did you not once mention a leader of the Grain-Boat Guild in Songjiang, an honest and capable man? Would he help Zhejiang?” “His surname is You. If you give the word, he will gladly serve. But what form would his help take?”

『自然是带队伍缉私。』胡雪岩是明知故问；等左宗棠有了答复，因话答话，故意摇摇头说∶『这怕办不到。他本人是个「运子」，不是官儿的身分；说到规矩，见了把总都要尊称一声「总爷」。大人请想，他怎么带队伍？就算他肯帮，分拨过示的官兵，也不服他的指挥。』『这话倒也是。』左宗棠踌躇了，『不过，若非带队伍缉私，又有什么可以借重他之处？』『漕帮的底蕴，大人向来深知。尤某的手下，都听他一句话∶如果有个名义，对松江一带的缉私，成效是一定有的。』『喔，我明白了。』左宗棠想了一会说∶『这样办也没有什么不可以；让尤某自己去招人，当然也不能太多，招个两三百人，保尤某一个官职，让他管带。这件事，我交代盐运使去办；尤某那里，请你去接头。至于饷银公费，一概照我营里的规矩，由盐务经费里面开支。』胡雪岩很高兴；这不但为尤五找到了一条生路，而且于公事亦有裨益，所以欣然应诺。

“Naturally, he would lead troops against smugglers.” Hu had asked a question whose answer he knew. Now he deliberately shook his head. “I fear that cannot be done. He is a grain-transport boatman, not an official. By the rules of rank he must address even a bazong respectfully as ‘sir.’ How could he command troops? Even if he agreed, the officers and men assigned to him would not obey.” “True.” Zuo hesitated. “But unless he leads troops against smugglers, how can we make use of him?” “You know the workings of the guild well. His followers all obey his word. Give him an official capacity, and there will certainly be results against smuggling around Songjiang.” “Ah, I understand.” After a moment Zuo said, “There is no objection to that. Let him recruit his own men—not too many, of course; two or three hundred will do. We shall recommend him for an official rank and let him command them. I shall tell the salt commissioner to arrange it. Please make contact with You. Pay and operating expenses will follow the rules of my own army and come from the salt administration’s funds.” Hu was delighted. He had found a livelihood for Brother You and a means of serving public business at the same time. He gladly agreed.

然后谈到蒋益澧所托之事；亦就是浙江按月协解福建饷银的数目。『从前浙江靠福建协饷，前后用过三百万之多；如今浙师援闽，饷银自然应该由浙江接济。大人是怎么个主意，请交代下来，好趁早筹划。』『我已经跟芗泉谈妥当了，浙江每个月接济我二十万。』『二十万不多，只限浙江的元气丧得太厉害！』胡雪岩故意沉吟了一会；然后突如其来地问说∶『大人是不是打算到了福建，要奏调蒋杨两位去帮忙？』这话问得左宗棠莫名其妙，立即答说∶『我并没有这样的打算。而且蒋杨两位，也巴结到监司大员了，一则福建无可位置；二则，朝廷也未见得会准。再说，我又何苦为马谷山铺路，腾出这么两个紧要缺分，好方便他援引私人？』这番回答，原在胡雪岩意料之中；尤其是最后一点，更有关系——蒋益澧留任浙江藩司；并保杨昌为浙江阜司，原是左宗棠所下的一着『行手棋』，用来箝制马新贻，保护他在浙江的饷源，岂肯自我退让？而胡雪岩所以明知故问，亦正是因话答话，好引入正题的一种手法。『这就是了！但愿蒋杨二分，安于其位；就等于大人仍旧兼摄浙江抚篆一样。不过，大人，我有句话，只怕忠言逆耳。』『不要紧，你我无话不可谈。而况你必是为我打算的好话。』

They next turned to the business Jiang Yili had entrusted to Hu: Zhejiang’s monthly contribution to the army in Fujian. “Zhejiang formerly depended on Fujian for more than three million taels,” Hu began. “Now that Zhejiang troops are going to its aid, Zhejiang should naturally support them. What arrangement do you propose, my lord? We should know early enough to prepare.” “I have settled it with Xiangquan: Zhejiang will send me two hundred thousand a month.” “Two hundred thousand is not much. The trouble is that Zhejiang’s strength has been so badly drained.” Hu deliberately paused, then asked without warning, “Once you reach Fujian, do you intend to request the transfer of Jiang and Yang to assist you?” Zuo was baffled. “I have no such intention. Both have worked their way up to senior provincial office. For one thing, Fujian has no suitable positions; for another, the court might not approve. Besides, why should I clear the road for Ma Gushan, vacating two important posts so that he can bring in his own men?” Hu had expected this answer, particularly the last point. Keeping Jiang as provincial treasurer and recommending Yang Changjun as judicial commissioner was a calculated move to restrain Ma and protect Zuo’s revenue in Zhejiang. Why would Zuo surrender that advantage? Hu had asked precisely to lead the conversation toward his real purpose. “Exactly. If Jiang and Yang remain secure in their posts, it will be almost as though you still held the acting governorship. But I fear I must offer some unwelcome advice.” “Go ahead. There is nothing you and I cannot discuss. Besides, I know it will be for my good.”

『是，我是替大人打算；细水长流，稳扎稳打。』胡雪岩很从容地答说∶『浙江的收入不但有限，而且没有确数可以预估。地丁钱粮，已经奉旨豁免；盐课收入，决要明年春末夏初，才有起色；米捐要看邻省肯不肯帮忙？靠得住的，只有厘金；市面越来越兴旺，收数自然越来越多，但也要看经手人的操守。至于支出，第一是善后；第二是海塘，都要大把花银子。大小衙门，文武官员的经费俸禄，更不能不筹；地方上总还要养些兵。大人倒想一想看，倘或每个月先凑二十万银子解粮台；藩库一清如洗，什么事都动不了，蒋芗泉这个藩司，怎么还当得下去？』『这，』左宗棠呆了半晌，方始说下去∶『这也不致于如你所说的那样子艰窘吧？』『当然。我是说得过分了一点。不过，大人，请你也要替马中丞想一想；人家刚刚巴结到方面大员，自然也想做番事业。如果处处捉襟见肘，动弹不得；那时候怎么办？只有逼蒋芗泉；逼蒋芗泉就是逼大人。』胡雪岩停了一下又说∶『从前江西沈中丞是曾中堂一手提拔的；本省的厘金说截留就截留，朝廷也不曾责备他耽误了曾家弟兄的「东征」。马中丞为人虽不如沈中丞那样子刚烈，然而也不是肯得过且过的人。』提到沈葆桢与曾国藩交恶的往事，左宗棠不能不起警惕之心。他是最讲究利害关系；冷静思量，马新贻的脚步站得很稳；亦无弱点可攻，果然为此有所争执，自己不见得能占上风。而且一闹开来，蒋益澧首当其冲；他一调离了浙江，每月又何有二十万银子可得？转念以此，便心平气和地问道∶『那末，雪岩，你说呢？我该怎么办？』

“Yes, I am thinking of your interests: a small but steady stream, a firm and lasting arrangement,” Hu replied calmly. “Zhejiang’s income is not merely limited; it cannot yet be estimated with certainty. The land-tax payments have been remitted by imperial order. Salt revenue will not improve before late spring or early summer next year. The rice levy depends upon neighboring provinces’ willingness to help. Only likin can be relied upon. As trade revives, receipts should increase, though even that depends upon the honesty of the collectors. On the expenditure side, reconstruction comes first, and the sea dikes second; both require great sums. Government offices and civil and military salaries must also be provided for, and the province must maintain some troops of its own. Suppose two hundred thousand taels is scraped together each month and sent first to your supply bureau, leaving the provincial treasury bare and all other work at a standstill. How could Jiang Xiangquan remain treasurer?” “Surely—” Zuo was silent for a while. “Surely things cannot be as difficult as you suggest?” “Of course. I have overstated them a little. But consider Governor Ma too. Having just risen to provincial authority, he naturally wishes to accomplish something. If he is hampered on every side, what can he do but press Jiang? And to press Jiang is to press you.” Hu paused. “Governor Shen of Jiangxi owed his advancement entirely to Grand Secretary Zeng. Yet he withheld his province’s likin revenues when he chose, and the court did not blame him for delaying the Zeng brothers’ eastern campaign. Governor Ma may not be as fierce as Shen, but neither is he content merely to drift.” The example of Shen Baozhen’s rupture with Zeng put Zuo on his guard. No one paid closer attention to practical interests. Considered calmly, Ma’s position was secure and offered no weakness to attack. If a dispute arose, Zuo might not prevail. Jiang would bear the first blow; once removed from Zhejiang, how could he provide two hundred thousand a month? With this thought, Zuo asked in a more even temper, “Then what do you advise, Xueyan?”

胡雪岩率直答道∶『只有减个数目。』『减多少呢？』左宗棠问。『这我就不敢说了。』左宗棠答道，『惟有请大人交代下去，官兵弟兄先委屈些，只要局面一好转，必然补报。』『好！』左宗棠点点头，『我也不忍太累浙江；就照你的意思，让粮台重新核算，减到减无可减为止。不过，雪岩，我的处境你是知道的，一直孤立无援；总要打开一条出路才好。』『是！』胡雪岩毫无表情地应声。『你要大大地帮我的忙！』左宗棠问道，『你看，我的出路该怎么打？』『大人不是已有成算了吗？』那是指谋取广东而言。左宗棠微微皱着眉说∶『驱郭不难；难在执可取代？芗泉的资望，当方面之任，总嫌不足。万一碰个钉子，我以后就难说话了。这一层关系很大，没有把握以前，我不便贸然动手。然而，这话又不能向芗泉透露。』胡雪岩很用心地听着；细细体会，辩出味外之味，蒋益澧如果想当广东巡抚，不得另外去找一份助力。这也就是说，只要朝中有奥援，保证左宗棠将来举荐时不会驳回；他是乐于出奏的。

“The amount must be reduced,” Hu answered directly. “By how much?” “I dare not fix a figure. You must ask the officers and men to bear some hardship for the present. Once matters improve, they can be compensated.” “Very well.” Zuo nodded. “I too cannot bear to overburden Zhejiang. As you suggest, I shall have the supply bureau recalculate and reduce the sum as far as possible. But you know my position. I have always been isolated and unsupported. I must open a way forward.” “Yes,” Hu answered without expression. “You must help me greatly. How do you think I should find that way?” “Have you not already decided, my lord?” He meant the plan to gain control of Guangdong. Zuo frowned slightly. “Removing Guo is not difficult. The question is who can replace him. Xiangquan still lacks the standing for a governorship. If my recommendation is rejected, I shall find it hard to speak again. The consequences are serious. I cannot act rashly before I am sure. Yet I cannot tell Xiangquan this.” Hu listened closely, searching beneath the words. If Jiang wanted Guangdong, he would need another source of support. In other words, if influential patrons at court could ensure that the recommendation would succeed, Zuo would gladly submit it.

想到这里，便又自问∶是不是该帮帮蒋益澧的忙？这个忙帮得上帮不上？前者无须多作考虑；能让蒋益澧调升广东巡抚，于公于私都大有好处。至于帮得上忙、帮不上忙？此时言之过早；反正事在人为，只要尽力，就有希望。想停当随即说道∶『大人是朝廷柱石，圣眷一直优隆。我在上海听京里的人说起，恭王很看重大人；醇王尤其佩服。想当初，曾中堂可以保他督办军务有关省份的巡抚；如今大人又为什么不可以？至于说到芗泉的资望，由浙藩升粤抚，亦不算躐等；马中丞不就是个现成的例子？当然，广东因为粤海关的收入与内务府很有关系，情形与他省不同；但是，只要京里有人照应，亦不是没有希望的事。』『就是这话罗，要京里有人照应！芗泉在这一层上头，比较吃亏。』『就眼前烧起冷灶来，也还不晚。』左宗棠深看了他一眼；沉吟又沉吟，终于说了一句∶『你不妨与芗泉谈谈！』『是！』

Hu then asked himself whether he should help Jiang and whether he could. The first question required little thought: Jiang’s promotion to Guangdong would bring great public and private advantages. As for whether help was possible, it was too early to say. Much depended upon effort; if he did his utmost, there was hope. “You are a pillar of the court, my lord, and have always enjoyed great imperial favor,” he said. “In Shanghai I heard from people newly arrived from Beijing that Prince Gong values you highly, and Prince Chun admires you still more. Grand Secretary Zeng was allowed to recommend governors for provinces within his military command. Why should you not have the same right? As for Xiangquan’s standing, promotion from Treasurer of Zhejiang to Governor of Guangdong would be no extraordinary leap. Governor Ma is an example ready to hand. Guangdong is different because its maritime customs revenues are closely connected with the Imperial Household Department. Still, if someone in Beijing looks after the matter, there is hope.” “Exactly—someone in Beijing must look after it. Xiangquan is at a disadvantage there.” “It is not too late to begin tending those neglected fires.” Zuo looked at him intently, pondered for some time, then finally said, “You might discuss it with Xiangquan.” “Yes.”

『他的事要靠你。』左宗棠又说，『我更少你不得。你在我这里，既不带兵，又不管粮台；可是比带兵管粮台更要紧。雪岩，等我一走，你也要赶紧动身，长驻上海；粮台接济不上，要饷要粮要军装，我就只靠你一个人了！』这份责任太重，胡雪岩顿感双肩吃力；可是说什么也不能有所犹豫，便硬着头皮答一声∶『是！大人请放心！』『有你这句话，我真的可以放心了。』左宗棠舒了口气；然后问道∶『你有什么事，要我替你办的？我预备月底动身；还有半个月的功夫。有话你趁早说。』胡雪岩早就想过了，左宗棠一走，虽是蒋益澧护理巡抚的大印，有事仍旧可以商量得通；然而究竟不如托左宗棠来得简捷有力。这半年的相处，自己从无一事求他；如今却不能再错过机会了。更何况是他先开口相问；倘再不言，反显得矫饰虚伪，未免太不聪明。

“He must rely on you,” Zuo continued. “And I can do without you even less. You command no troops for me and run no supply bureau, yet your work is more important than either. Once I leave, you must set out promptly and remain in Shanghai. If the supply bureau falls short—whether of pay, grain, or military equipment—you alone will be my resource.” The responsibility weighed heavily upon Hu, but he could show no hesitation. He braced himself. “Yes, my lord. You may be at ease.” “With that assurance, I truly can.” Zuo breathed out, then asked, “What would you like me to do for you? I intend to leave at the end of the month; there is still half a month. If you want anything, tell me early.” Hu had already considered this. After Zuo left, Jiang would hold the acting governor’s seal and could still be consulted; yet a request to Zuo would be more direct and effective. During their half-year together, Hu had asked no favor. He must not miss the opportunity now, especially when Zuo himself had invited him to speak. Further silence would seem affected and false, and would hardly be wise.

有此了解，便决定『畅所欲言』；先使个以退为进的手法，『想求大人的事情很多，』他说，『又怕大人厌烦，不敢多说。』『不要紧，不要紧！』左宗棠连连摆手，『一向都是我托你，欠你的情很多；你尽管说。』『是！』胡雪岩说∶『第一件，从前的王中丞，死得太惨。当时蒙大人主持公道，查明经过，查明参奏。不过这一案还没有了，想请大人始终成全。』『喔，』左宗棠有些茫然；因为事隔两年有余，记忆不清，只好问说∶『这一案怎么没有了？』

He decided to speak freely, first retreating a little in order to advance. “There are many things I wish to ask, but I fear you may find them tiresome.” “Not at all!” Zuo waved both hands. “I am always asking you for help and owe you many favors. Speak.” “First, the former Governor Wang died so tragically. You upheld justice, investigated what had happened, and reported the facts to the throne. But the case is not finished. I should like you to see it through.” “Oh?” More than two years had passed, and Zuo’s recollection was vague. “In what way is it unfinished?”

『就是同治元年四月里，大人所奏的「讯明王履谦贻误情形」那一案——』『啊，』左宗棠被提醒了，『你等一下。』他欣开马褂，从腰带上去取钥匙——钥匙表示权威，大而至于『神机营』、『内务府』，被指定为『蒙明』，即表示赋予首脑之任；小而至于一家大户人家的管家——或者象红楼梦中的王熙凤，都以掌管钥匙为实权在握的鲜明表示。只是钥匙甚小，不瞳以显示其权威的地位，所以多加上些附丽之物；通常都是『以多取胜』，弄些根本无用的钥匙拴在一起；甚至弄个大铁环串连，拎在手里『蒋朗蒋朗』地响，仿佛『牢头禁子』的用心，只要拎着那串钥匙一抖动，就足以慑服群囚。可是，真正能见钥匙之重的，却往往只有一枚，左宗棠亦是如此，他只有一枚钥匙，用根丝绳子穿起，挂在腰带上；此时往外一拉，以身相就，凑近一个书箱，打开来取出一大叠红簿册；胡雪岩遥遥望去，只见上面写着四个大字∶『奏稿留底』。检到同治元年四月的那一本，左宗棠戴上墨晶老花眼镜细看了一遍，方始发问∶『雪岩，你说此案未了；未了的是什么？』

“I mean your memorial in the fourth month of the first Tongzhi year, reporting the inquiry into Wang Lüqian’s obstruction and failures—” “Ah!” Reminded, Zuo said, “Wait a moment.” He lifted his riding jacket and took a key from his belt. Keys signified authority. In institutions as great as the Shenji Camp or the Imperial Household Department, to be designated keeper of the keys meant being entrusted with leadership. In a wealthy household, a steward—or Wang Xifeng in Dream of the Red Chamber—likewise displayed practical power by holding the keys. A key was small, however, insufficiently imposing to proclaim such authority. Hence the additions: usually quantity made the impression. Useless keys were tied together, sometimes threaded on a large iron ring that clattered in the hand. The intention resembled a jailer’s: shake the bunch, and every prisoner would submit. Yet the truly weighty key was often a single one. Zuo had only one, threaded on a silk cord at his belt. Pulling it out, he leaned toward a book chest, unlocked it, and removed a thick stack of red booklets. From a distance Hu could read the large characters on their covers: “Copies of Memorials.” Zuo found the booklet for the fourth month of the first Tongzhi year, put on his smoky-crystal reading spectacles, and studied it before asking, “What remains unsettled, Xueyan?”

『请大人再检当时的批回；就知道了。』批回一时无从检取，左宗棠答说∶『想来你总清楚，说给我听吧！』『是！』胡雪岩倒有些为难了。

“If you look at the reply received then, my lord, you will see.” The reply could not readily be found. “You must know what it said. Tell me.” “Yes.” Hu now felt awkward.

因为当王有龄苦守杭州时，主要的饷源是在绍兴；而在籍团练大臣王履谦，却不甚合作。同时绍兴有些擅于刀笔的劣绅，包围王履谦，视王有龄以一省大吏征饷为不恤民困，勒索自肥，无形中官民之间竟成了敌对的局面。因此，绍兴府知府廖宗元的处境极其困难；当长毛由萧山往绍兴进攻时，官军的炮船与团练竟发生了冲突。兵力悬殊，寡不敌众，廖宗元的亲兵被杀了十二个；廖宗元本人亦被打破了头。这本来是应该由王履谦去弹压排解的，而居然袖手旁观。不久，绍兴沦陷；廖宗元殉难；而王履谦则先期逃到宁波，出海避难在福建。绍兴不该失而失，以及王履谦的处处掣肘，不顾大局，使王有龄深恶痛绝，在危城中寄出来的血书，表示『死不瞑目』。胡雪岩亦就因为如此，耿耿于怀，一直想为王有龄报仇雪恨。

When Wang Youling had held Hangzhou through the siege, his principal source of funds had been Shaoxing. Wang Lüqian, the militia commissioner residing there, had been uncooperative. Unscrupulous local gentry, skilled with their pens, surrounded him and portrayed the governor’s demands for military funds as callous extortion for private gain. Officials and people had almost imperceptibly become enemies. This made the position of Prefect Liao Zongyuan extremely difficult.
